Born in the subterranean cities of Calth, Uriel Ventris went on to earn the command of the Chapter's 4th Company and Fleet, and became one of the Ultramarines' greatest heroes.
Little is hidden from Tigurius' sight. Even to the Chapter's Captains he is a figure of mystery, possessed of a knowledge well beyond the Imperium's towering archives.
Ever since the times of the Great Crusade, the Ultramarines have been amongst the most renowned of the Imperium's forces, accruing uncountable battle honours through the millennia.
The return of Guilliman during one of Mankind's darkest times returned a glimmer of hope to the hearts of humanity, kindling a light that would guide the Imperium into a new era.
The Ultramarines strict adherence to the Codex Astartes is what makes the Chapter amongst the most highly organized forces in the Imperium.
After Guilliman's revision of the Codex Astartes, the rank of Lieutenant was reintroduced. Lieutenants now lead their battle-brothers as they did during the Horus Heresy.
Though famed as a general, Marneus Calgar is no stranger to personal valour. The Lord Macragge leads by example, inspiring his warriors from the heart of the enemy's lines.
Calgar is often regarded as Mankind's will to endure and triumph made flesh. Staunch and determined, he will lead the fight from the front until the stars turn cold.
Since earning his monicker by disfiguring Krugg the Tyrant in a bout for leadership, Grukk's utterly brutal way of fighting has only worsened, to the terror of his enemies.
To prove their worth before the eyes of their brutal and cunning gods, the mighty Ghazghkull has gathered the largest Waaagh recorded in millennia.
Strength and brutality are paramount in Ork kultur, where any argument is bound to cause a fight. Ghazghkull is the greatest ork debater, having never lost a discussion.
Ork Warbosess who revere Mork, the more cunning of Ork gods, occasionally think through their battle plans before plunging headlong into battle.
Orks never stop growing. Bigger orks tend to rule over smaller ones, having achieved victory in many battles and survived violent challenges to their position.
Orks believe that Ghazghkull receives messages from Gork and Mork themselves, and that with him in command of 'Da Great Waaagh' they will turn the stars green.
After Ghazghkull's many fights with Commissar Yarrick on Armageddon, Ghazghkull left the world infested with scattered greenskins and vowing to one day return.
Known as simply 'Da Boss' to his Vulcha Squad, Zagstruk inspires close to fanatical awe among Stormboyz, who queue up to follow his bellowed commands.
It is the simple and resilient nature of Ork society that raises them from a civilisation of mere thuggish beasts to a world-conquering, nigh on unstoppable threat.
Mekboyz and Painboyz can get really collaborative. Mekboyz fashion combat walkers known as Deff Dreads, then the Painboyz work with them to wire ‘volunteers’ into the war engines.
The stars speak of what is to come. Reading them, Orikan has divined the future of the Necrons, and once they are in proper alignment, he will finally embrace his true destiny.
The words and actions of Chronomancers bear vast weight, as knowledge of the future flows through them. The future is fickle, but the stars will guide the Necrons to a new golden age.
Uncountable legions and war machines at their command, ready to devastate the enemy in the blink of an eye. Thus shall Necron Overlords reclaim the Galaxy.
Entombed for millions of years, the Necrons slumbered through the aeons. Now stirring back to life across the galaxy, their unstoppable Legions are rising.
Aeons ago, a great war against the Aeldari forced the Necrons into a period of slumber. Now it comes to an end, and so shall the ancient ruling dynasties be restored.
Imotekh's aims to restore the Necron Empire to its former glory. Only when the dynasties are united as one will Necron dominance over inferior beings begin anew.
After taking the thron from a nobility focused on their own petty squabbles, Imotekh shaped the destiny of his awakening dynasty, ensuring their dominance over the lesser races.
The title of nemesor is a weighty one. Even after the strain of revivification, Zahndrekh still stands as one of the greatest Sautekh strategists, and a champion of its dynastic code.
Through their advanced knowledge of science and technology, Necron Crypteks manipulate many of the universe's primordial forces to produce seemingly sorcerous effects.
The arrival of the Worldclaimer heralds certain doom to any foe. It is he who proclaims the death of worlds, and he who drives his spear through citizen and warrior alike.
True to his Word Bearers origins, Sylar's gift with words goes beyond mortal imagination. With his incantations, Hexscorn channels daemonic powers to those under his command.
The Black Legion was formed from the hosts of many warbands and warlords. All would swear allegiance to Abaddon, who leads them with absolute dominion.
The Eye of Terror became the sanctuary of the traitor Legions after the Horus Heresy, and a place for the Black Legion to gather its forces in preparation for a Black Crusade.
From shame and shadow recast, in black and gold reborn. In Abaddon, the forces of Chaos saw a new Warmaster to lead them to claim the final victory they were denied so long ago.
The latest of Abaddon's Black Crusades ended with the destruction of Cadia and the opening of the Great Rift, a massive tear in reality that broke the Imperium in two.
After the 13th Black Crusade, Abaddon became the master of the sundered half of Humanity's realm that was, he said, far more territory than Horus ever conquered and held.
There was a time in which the Eye of Horus represented the Emperor's eternal vigilance. Those days are long gone, and this is now a symbol of dread and despair.
Since the end of the Horus Heresy, Abaddon has gathered the scattered forces of Chaos under his banner. He is determined to claim vengeance against the False Emperor.
Anvirr's prescient abilities brought him to Vigilus, where he struck an unlikely alliance with Marneus Calgar to fend off a Chaos armada that threatened the future of the Aeldari.
Protector of the Craftworld, Ghaelyn has risen her spear against shadow and flame time and again, commanding Saim-Hann's forces in defence of Aeldari sanctuaries and Maiden Worlds.
Each member of a Saim-Hann Wild Host longs to be the first into the fight, the one to claim first blood's glory. Nothing will stand between them and their quarry.
The stars are aligned, and the crimson moon tells the hour of blood and clashing blades has come. It is time for the Wild Host to rise and ride, time for the serpent to bite.
All Aeldari can manipulate psychic energies to a degree. Much of their wargear is crafted is empathically linked to the user, who can activate it with a mere thought.
Saim-Hann symbology is reminiscent of the Cosmic Serpent, the creature believed to exist in both the material and the psychic universes at the same time in Aeldari Myth.
Nearly all Saim-Hann belong to a Wild Rider clan, who ride in jetbike squads comprised of blood relatives, sporting banners with their clan runes as they cut down enemy lines.
It is a painful irony that, in the Aeldari's endless quest for survival, the very civilians the warhosts fight to protect are all too often forced to take up arms themselves.
With shocking agility and precision, the warhosts of Eliac Zephyrblade rain down like the spears of Khaine against the heart of those who dare harm the Craftworld.
Psychic prowess made form, the Neurothrope acts not only as a synapse node, but as a pulsing psychic nexus, channeling eldritch forces to leech the life of its foes.
Tervigons make sure that the onslaught never ends, awakening the dormant Termagants they carry in their abdomen, and tearing enemies apart with their claws.
The hardened chitin that frames the forms of the tyranids has proven unnaturally durable. Few can stop the swarm once it is determined to devour a planet.
Hive Fleet Leviathan has spread its tendrils through the Galaxy, ready to consume all in its path. All who encounter them fear that there is no stopping the Great Devourer.
Settling like a vast and terrible pall across countless worlds, the Shadow in the Warp is a nightmarish phenomenon that heralds the coming of the Tyranid hive fleets.
The Hive Mind is the gestalt collective consciousness of its species, an unfathomable intelligence created by the psychic presence of billions of Tyranids all connected to each other.
The Swarmlord's characteristic weapons can slice through adamantium and protective fields as if they were nothing. They lash out with such speed that few even get a chance to strike.
A uniquely powerful galactic threat, the Swarmlord is the most powerful synapse creature ever known, undying and as old as the Tyranid species itself.
The first warning most worlds have of the Tyranids’ approach is the Shadow in the Warp. This psychic signal rolls ahead of the hive fleets like a smothering metaphysical fog bank.
A Tyranid attack is a harrowing spectacle to behold. Vast swarms of ravenous monsters flow across the land, slaughtering all in their path.
From the darkness between the stars they flow, a tide of living nightmares. Their shadow is the funeral shroud of civilisations. Their hunger is the death of worlds.
The T’au Sept is the blazing beacon for the light of the Greater Good and their greatest seat of culture and wisdom, as well as a byword for military excellence.
The XV8 Crisis provided the prototype chassis for several more advanced battlesuits, including the XV86 Coldstar with its trans-atmospheric flight capabilities.
Adherents of the T'au'va gladly expend incredible efforts, endure shocking hardships and lay down their lives without a second thought for the furtherance of the Greater Good.
The T'au believe the message of the Greater Good must be brought to all, so they keep growing their empire’s borders and establishing new colonised systems called septs.
Developed in secret upon J'ka'vo Station and each piloted by a handpicked Shas'vre, Ghostkeel Battlesuits embarked upon numerous covert operations before their official unveiling
The Kroot are warlike and bloodthirsty warriors. Although their primitive aggression is viewed with distaste by the T’au, such inherent savagery makes them effective shock troops.
The Ethereal Caste stand apart from their people. They rule the T’au as a wise and patient adult might guide spirited, wayward youths to realise their truest potential.
Shadowsun has rendered the advanced XV22 Stalker Battlesuit iconic, becoming so adroit at operating it that it is to her now like an armoured second skin.
The Galaxy is merciless. If one seeks to survive its dangers, one must be prepared to overcome countless challenges. Will you withstand the whims of fate?
Every advancement in warfare requires a proper field test, and those willing to aid in pushing the boundaries of what is possible will rise in the Omnissiah's grace.
History is ruled by cause and effect. The ripples sent by events from eras long gone can still be felt all through the Galaxy. Will your deeds also echo through eternity?
Some traitors have given themselves entirely to the service of the Dark Gods, and they are so lost to damnation that they barely resemble the warriors they once were.
The Dark Apostle’s prayers fill his followers’ hearts with hatred as they lash out with fanatical strength to tear down their foes in the Dark Gods’ names.
The Warp exists as a source of both limitless power and eternal damnation. Such power has ever tempted the unwary, the desperate and the ambitious into its bottomless depths.
The most tainted conjurations can be achieved with daemonic energy. Sorcerers may have been psykers from birth; others may be warriors granted such power by a daemonic patron.
The Sisters of the Order of Our Martyred Lady are the deliverers of the God-Emperor’s holy justice, the dreaded instruments of his will to whom no sacrifice is too great.
For the Adepta Sororitas the act of fighting in defence of their faith, against the foul heretics that would tear it down, is itself deemed a hallowed honour.
The Adepta Sororitas are a crusading military force that crushes the enemies of the Imperial Creed wherever they fester, illuminating the Emperor’s realm as a beacon of faith.
It is said that the blood of martyrs is the seed of the Imperium. Where it falls, repugnance and vengeance blossom, and the furious reprisals of the faithful thrive.
In the sepulchre of battle, they are the God-Emperor’s holiest warriors. In the reliquary of war, where saints are made and faith burns brightest, they are His will made manifest.
Shapers instinctively recognise desirable or detrimental biological traits in defeated foes, guiding their kindred's evolution and adaptation to future challenges.
Necrons replaced their fleshly weakness with enduring forms of living metal aeons ago. However, the biotransference also devoid most Necrons of their free will.
The Emperor protects the faithful from the corruption that lurks in the darkness. It is under His light that the Sororitas are driven onwards with indomitable will.
Declared by the reigning ecclesiarch of the Adeptus Ministorum, Wars of Faith are often called to seek the conquest of new territory or purge Heretics to the Imperial Creed.
The tenets of the Orders joyously proclaim the blood of martyrs is the life force of the Imperium, making the sacrifice of their fallen Sisters shine brightest in the darkest hour.
After the defeat of the Old Ones, when the C’tan were at their weakest following that titanic conflict, the Necrons took their revenge, shattering and imprisoning the duplicitous star gods.
Chaplains are fiery, strict and quickly roused to anger by the hated enemy. For all their grim demeanour, Chaplains care deeply for the spiritual well-being of their brothers.
Battle Companies are frequently split into two demi-companies each under the direct command of a Lieutenant, an extremely able tactician and highly skilled warrior.
Bolt weapons have been synonymous with the Space Marines since before even the Great Crusade. Countless foes have been laid low by their explosive rounds, known as bolts.
To the 4th Company falls the duty of defending wider Ultramar from the predations of the countless heretics, aliens and monstrosities who would see it torn down in flames.
Proud allies of the T'au Empire, the Kroot's rustic equipment and savage countenance perfectly depict their fearsome skill in combat.
"Give praise to the Star Children! Give praise to the Master Below! Give praise for deliverance, and freedom, and ascension!"
Genestealer Cults are dominated by a Patriarch via the synaptic link known as Broodmind. As the Cult grows, its Broodmind becomes a psychic beacon for the Tyranid hive.
In shadow they lurk, insidious, patient. Day by day they spread their curse. They syphon strength and dig their tendrils ever deeper, until by their word blood and horror unfolds.
Each gene-sect spontaneously spawns remarkable individuals with focused skills whose presence smoothens the road to ascension, each moulded by the world and culture it parasitises.
Since the first infection, successive generations will be born within the cult. Offspring born to the fourth generation are Purestrain Genestealers that will start the cycle anew.
Through cunning and fortune, Genestealer Cults send their questing tendrils writhing into even the highest ranks of the military forces that should be standing guard against it.
As the uprising bursts out, the Patriarch leaves its throne amidst its bubbling genesis pools and emerges from the shadows. The monstrous, parasitic demigod leads the final assault.
Offspring born to the fourth generation are Purestrain Genestealers. Their parents perceive their nightmare progeny as blessed cherubs, and would die for them in a heartbeat.
The people of the craftworlds adhere to a set of strictures known as the Path, or the Ai’elethra, mastering their whims through the rigid emotional discipline of the Path.
Meks are driven to constantly tinker and experiment with new ideas. They will gladly do kustom jobs for other Orks in return for payment in teef or looted scrap.
A skilled warrior on the battlefield, Titus' duty often sets him against impossible odds, with only his fury, resolve, and honed fighting abilities seeing him through.
Due to their failure to protect the dynastic codes by the end of the War in Heaven, Triarch Praeotrians were charged to watch over the slumbering tomb worlds during the Great Sleep.
Ramatekh exudes a soul-sapping presence. The promise of life’s end is so explicit in its chilling gaze that few can muster the strength of will to evade it.
Crypteks amass whole armies of artificial constructs and soulless soldiery to achieve their goal. Blindly loyal followers, these automata are guided by their masters’ ancient genius.
Regiments and their worlds of origin glorify the noble victories, last stands and epic crusades of their warriors by embroiding them in glorious, awe inspiring tapestries.
The Imperium is faced with many horrors. The soldiers of the Astra Militarum are the Hammer of the Emperor, and by their deeds shall the enemies of Mankind be destroyed.
Obliterating the enemies of the Imperium with explosive shells, armoured regiments are a punishingly effective and sometimes excessive response to invasion and insurrection.
They are the grist upon which the Imperium’s war machine turns. They are the anvil upon which victories are forged. They are the shield behind which Humanity shall endure.
During The Forging, as systems were brought into the Imperial fold, the Shock Troops of Cadia imparted their discipline and military doctrine to the leaders of newly colonised worlds.
With rifle, cannon and Human grit they throw back nightmarish horrors. They are the soldiers of the Astra Militarum, and in their unrecorded deaths is unsullied duty made manifest.
The Galaxy is merciless, yet the fearless few rise to claim their place in it. Given to those who commanded their decks to victory during the Early Access stage of Warpforge
Cadians have faith in Humanity's strength, yet they rely not solely on prayers for salvation. In their darkest hour, they face evil not pleading, but firing their weapon to the bitter end.
Most Asuryani eventually join the war voluntarily. Known as Warrior Aspects, each branch of the Path has its own unique fighting style and reflects a unique facet of the god Khaine.
Howling Banshees announce their arrival with a blood-chilling scream amplified by their Banshee masks, inflicting severe damage to the central nervous systems of their foes.
When Asurmen raised the original Aspect Warriors he became the first of the Asurya. First to learn under his tutelage was Jain Zar, an Aeldari swordmaiden famed for her speed and ferocity.
The Human race bears deep scars upon their collective psyche from the Age of Strife. Mankind survived its ravages fragmented and desperate, emerging as a species much changed.
Wreathed in holy light and possessed of divine serenity, the Sisters of the Sacred Rose are the calm at the centre of a violent storm.
Sisters of the Sacred Rose reflect the serene demeanor of their Matriarch, Arabella, renowned for her calm nature even in the face of horror.
The Orders of the Adepta Sororitas are divided amongst the Convent Sanctorum, based on Ophelia VII, and the Convent Prioris, which was built within the Ecclesiarchal Palace upon Holy Terra.
The Adepta Sororitas execute anyone who expresses doubt in the security of the Imperium. The Sisters of the Sacred Rose have fought the enemies of the faith with resoluteness of spirit.
A revered relic sword once held by Saint Arabella herself, Aveline Aboyé now wields the Thorn of the White Rose with resolve against the foes she was sworn to vanquish.
The Adeptus Astartes are heavily augmented post-humans; products of years of arduous training, agonising surgery and psycho-indoctrination which not all inductees will survive.
The towering storm shields of the Bladeguard are the work of many generations of serfs, and the force field generators they contain protect the bearer’s soul as much as their flesh.
Among the bloody fates of a Chaos champion is internment in the sarcophagus of a Helbrute, a looming engine of carnage with the firepower of a tank and the bloodlust of a daemon.
On every tier of their Chapter’s organisation the Dark Angels have a baffling array of ancient rites and traditions led by the Dark Angels Chaplains, such as the Feast of Malediction.
Rededicated to serving the Imperium after eluding its heavy scrutiny, the Dark Angels enacted a plan to ensure the Legion survived. No one could doubt their resolve or commitment.
Believing their traitorous brothers perished in Caliban’s destruction, Dark Angels Librarians later discovered the psychic signatures of the Fallen, revealing they still lived.

After the destruction of Caliban, the Dark Angels thought themselves to be wholly guilty, and that should anyone learn of what had occurred, the First Legion would be declared Excommunicate Traitoris.
Since the times of the Great Crusade, the sons of Caliban have been at the forefront of some of the galaxy’s most significant wars, and have bled their foes in numerous war zones.
The Dark Angels’ deepest history is shrouded in mystery, not merely due to being thousands of years in the past, but also by Dark Angels’ Masters and Veterans deliberately obscuring it.
The proud warriors of the Dark Angels stubbornly refuse to accept defeat. Descendants of the First Legion, they stand foremost amongst the Space Marine Chapters.
The Dark Angels outfit their entire 1st Company – the Deathwing – with Terminator armour, lightning-wreathed power weapons and towering relic shields.

The Dark Angels were the First Legion. No other Space Marine brotherhood has served the Emperor for as long as they have. Staunch defenders of Mankind, they are merciless in the attack and stubborn in the defence.
Foremost in the Jackal's efforts is the Jackal Alphus. They possess the constitution to travel for days, planning and executing the perfect shot to eliminate key targets.
Whether hewing riches from hellish pits or toiling in forges, the faithful have become experts in handling the outsized industrial tools they now wield as weapons.
The Patriarch's telepathic urging implants the true goal in its broodkin: breach enemy lines and amass vital military intelligence. Then, the cult wreaks havoc with contrived wreckage.
Shock assault troops without peer, Tempestus Scions are elite soldiers used to enact missions that the regular Imperial Guard cannot accomplish alone.
From youth, Tempestus Scions are indoctrinated on loyalty and the swift execution of their duties. They possess the tenacity to undertake the toughest missions and get the job done.
Aquilons are trained to drop right into the thick of fighting. Their extensive conditioning allows them to stay focused even during the most ferocious insertions.
Some Orks are driven to leave their tribes and explore the wilds. Isolated Ork enclaves often devolve to a more primitive state and taken to squig-breeding, becoming Beast Snaggas.
The untameable squig; the Badbeast of Skrapmud– Big Chompa became Mozrog’s steed with a reputation for being the meanest and most savage creature ever to crawl from the drops.
Swallowed whole, half-digested, yet still krumpin', Mozrog Skragbad doesn't just hunt beasts. With an impressive tally of trophies, he is always driven to seek bigger quarry.
Beast Snaggas breed countless varieties of squigs: squigs for riding; squigs for eating; squigs from which to squeeze oil; squigs to send with hastily scrawled message glyphs...
Dangerous and unstable, Wurrboys are treated like oracles. Rarely lucid, they rant about visions of prey and lose themselves in the senses of their warband’s squigs.
After ten millennia, the fractured Emperor's Children still prey upon the galaxy in vibrant warbands of imperious skill, extravagant firepower, and ruinous desires.
Warfare is a blood-drenched art. Each battle is a fresh canvas upon which the superiority of Fulgrim's scions is depicted in gore, viscera and the agonised screams of the enemy.
The Emperor's Children's ingrained desire for sensation in all its forms sees them move rapidly across the battlefield to satiate their never-ending hunger for fresh experience.
When the Emperor's Children go to war, it is to the excruciating shriek of an array of outlandish sonic weaponry that splinters reality and rasps at the nerves of all who hear it.
Excess and obsession are the domains of Slaanesh. Unfulfilled desires and compulsive dreams are the cracks through which Slaanesh whispers' slip, luring mortals into their worship.
Born of Fulgrim’s gene-seed, the III Legion sought perfection in war. Hardened by a lifetime of ceaseless conflict, their pursuit of excellence slid into excess and damnation.
The Emperor's Children pursue exotic essences to feed their obsessions. Found in flesh, mind, and soul, they harvest torment to distill exquisite substances.
Seeking to commit ever more depraved atrocities to fulfill their monstrous desires, a warband's warriors may flay the skin from their victims with sharp blades or scintillating empyric sorcery.
Whether bending a daemon to their will or dominating an enemy champion, Lord Exultants revel in displaying their superiority and expose their foe's unforgivable flaws.
Lhykhis embodies Khaine's willingness to risk all to defeat the foe. She is amongst the most active Phoenix Lords, travelling far and wide in defence of the Asuryani.
Warp Spiders brave the Warp to defend the living, just as the tiny warp creatures to which they owe their name materialise near the Infinite Circuit to protect the dead.
The souls that pilot Asuryani wraith constructs experience reality as a dream, where their thoughts, feelings, and those of other Aeldari are as tangible as steel.
The proud warriors of the Dark Angels stubbornly refuse to accept defeat. Descendants of the First Legion, they stand foremost amongst the Space Marine Chapters.
The hour of blood and clashing blades has come.
I am tested time and time again and yet I prevail.
Each one of your vile deeds begets a dire consequence.
There is always a way. I always find it.
Never engage in a battle if you have not seen the outcome
I know what it is to lose everything, and I shall not falter.
You walk a path that leads to your own ruin.

Prayer is not a mere rite but a blade to be wielded. Muster your Faith to deal devastating blows unto the unsuspecting enemy.
Lead the condemned and the repentant to deliverance with a fearless and violent assault headlong towards the enemy.
Wage Wars of Faith with the most zealous and fervent Sisters. Purge the unclean and slay the heretic with the most aggressive units in your ranks.
Strike from the shadows and overrun your enemy with invisible blows. Harness deception and strike with formidable force before the foe can react.
As the Cult casts off its cloak of shadows in a full-scale uprising, its many claws strike as one. Rally your broodkin and overthrow the oppressor!
The Day of Ascension has come. Unleash your forces in open insurrection to overwhelm your enemy and receive the divine favour of the Star Children.
Sabotage the enemy's supply lines and prepare to unleash the full might of the Cult when the opportunity arises.
Deploy your forces covertly and ambush your unsuspecting enemies. Keep them off balance until the Cult's greatest threats rise to deliver the final blow.
Engage in subterfuge and sabotage operations to unravel your enemy's schemes. Command the battlefield with a tight grip, awaiting the perfect moment to strike.
Flood the battlefield with your shock troops and overwhelm the enemy in quick, unrelentless attacks.
When all seems lost there's still one undisputable answer: more firepower. Secure the battlefield with your tanks and artillery, before pushing forward for an overwhelming victory.
Carry your guardsmen to the frontline where they are needed most. Make good use of your armoured transports and find the opportunity to strike and claim victory.
Some battles are won by lightning fast attacks. Others become tests of attrition. Shield your key units and deploy massive firepower to overwhelm the helpless enemy!
Master the best qualities of your infantry and armoured companies to exert unbearable pressure on the enemy.
When every bullet counts, wise is the officer who shows no doubt, who leads their forces onward with conviction, pressing forward until the enemy frontline crumbles.
Hold off the enemy while your forces take on their missions, before smiting the opponent with the explosive might of the Dark Angels.
Prizing speed and mobility above all else, the Ravenwing are integral to the Dark Angels’ combat strategies. Use their unmatched speed to ravage the foe in a quick assault.
The Deathwing can manifest onto the battlefield with unerring accuracy, delivering the death blow to an enemy already ravaged by the Unforgiven forces.
The Inner Circle fights with privileged insight, striking at the precise moment and location required to tip the balance of battle.
The Ravenwing seek to encircle their foe, corralling them with methodical manoeuvres and target selection and ensuring noone can escape from their hunt.
The Deathwing Terminators often wait in teleportariums, ready to strike. Upon arrival, devastation follows in their wake.
Indulgence is their weapon, and agony its vessel. Poison the battlefield with suffering and sap the enemy’s will with every exquisite drop of torment.
Orchestrate excruciating aural barrages to shatter the most resilient defensive lines using the Emperor's Children's signature sonic weaponry.
Refined through pain, the Emperor’s Children strike with alchemical precision. Enhance your warriors with potent elixirs to turn every skirmish into a brutal performance.
Blessed by ruinous powers, the III Legion fights alongside Daemons of the Dark Prince, offering devotion in flesh, torment and suffering.
Every strike, every motion, every death—flawless. Lead with elegance and exacting control, overwhelming the enemy beneath a mask of immaculate violence.
Keep the pressure to satisfy the Emperor's Children's hunger for sensation, driving your forces to ever more depraved bloodshed by the offering of boons and exotic elixirs.

Ghazghkull Mag Uruk Thraka is a mighty prophet of the Waaagh! He is the most influential greenskin in the galaxy, and commands billions to war.
Boss of a band of Stormboyz, Zagstruk is known for his ambition and his temper. He has a pair of bionic legs called Da Vulcha’s Klaws, which he uses to rip his foes apart.
Grukk Face-Rippa is huge, even by Ork warboss standards. He is known for his giant power klaw and a temper that has started countless wars.
Cannon fodder, living shields, mine-field sweepers, emergency rations... A cunning Grot will always have a place and opportunities in Ork society.
Ghazghkull's official banner-waver. Makari is considered the luckiest grot alive, after surviving nine whole years next to Ghazghkull and being reincarnated multiple times.
In a rare flash of genius, the Orks discovered that the only thing needed to make Squigs more destructive was to fit as many explosives as possible on them.
Rough and tough to their core, Ork Boyz are the mainstay of Ork Mobs. At the shout of "WAAAGH!" these mobs will charge forward against the enemy in a flurry of gore and violence.
Tough and determined, these Orks are carried by Trukks, heavy transport vehicles capable of dropping whole mobs where they can do their best choppin'.
Stormboyz use rokkit packs to hurl themselves into battle. Braking systems are rare in Ork gadgets, so they will only stop when hitting an enemy, a wall or running out of fuel.
Capable of both chopin' and shootin', these versatile boyz charge while unleashing a flurry of bullets with their Sluggas and finish the job up close and personal.
The Hornhelmz were one of the battle-hardened mobs at the core of Ghazghkull’s Waaagh! during the first invasion of Armageddon.
Even if they disregard marksmanship, there is nothing orks love more than good "dakka". This is likely due to their enjoyment of the violent noise and recoil of automated gunfire.
Due to their aggressive nature it is inevitable for Orks to receive many scars. Veteran Orks show off their scars with pride and arrogance as a symbol of status.
Lootaz steal and scavenge enemy weaponry to gather bits and pieces for the Meks, who use this material to build, among other things, the Deffguns that Lootas use in battle.
The most respected Nobs carry the warband's banner into battle. Banner Nobs are inspiring and fearsome in combat, especially when they learn the banner can be used as a weapon.
Mekboys are in charge of creating the greatest "dakka" and mantaining all of the Ork's vehicles and weaponry. Without them, Orks would lack much of their fighting power.
The Orks that other Orks are scared of. Burna Boyz are lunatics that will set anything or anyone on fire for the simple joy of watching them "do the burny dance".
Orks prefer direct solutions, such as huge, armoured, hydraulic killing-klaws. Orks who get obsessed with this way of war are known as Big Krumpaz.
Orks will only seek help from Painboyz when they have no other choice. Returning to the battlefield is often more appealing than a Painboy's anesthesia, also known as a concussion.
The smallest of Ork combat walkers. After a volunteer Grot is forced into a Killa Kan and feels the rush of power, they often seek Orks that tormented him in the past for a rematch.
After a thunderous headbutt from Ghazghkull, Ugrak saw the light (many lights, actually) and decided to pledge his red power klaw to the hardest-hitting Warlord he had ever met.
Thrill-seeking Orks will never be satisfied by ground-based exhilaration. These individuals, considered unstable by other Orks, take to the skies in search of greater euphoria.
Only the hardest of the hard have what it takes to join Da Goff Guard of Ghazghkull Thraka. To spot 'Ardshell Gurk in battle, just look for the second biggest bloodbath.
Most Orks hate being knocked out before chopping a git during battle. Battlewagons solve that issue, carrying them into the front lines while shrugging off enemy fire.
Fairly compared to an armour-plated mountain covered in guns, the Stompa is a walking idol to Gork and Mork. These gargantuan war machines sometimes reach the size of a Reaver Titan.
Squigs are some of the most common Ork pets. As it's customary in Ork "Kultur", they can also be weaponized and thrown against an enemy.
Snotlings are unable to use Ork weaponry, which resulted in them occupying the lowest strata of Ork society. Still, do not trust any Orkoid near explosive material.
Orks display inhuman degrees of resilience and are able to withstand seemingly fatal wounds that would render many unable to fight with little to no long-term consequences.
After damaging his head with a Bolter shell, Ghazghkull believes Gork and Mork provide him with the information to conquer the Galaxy and turn the stars green.
Ork "Kultur" above all else is based entirely around fighting. As a Warboss earns victories, he also gains respect and increases the number of boyz he commands in battle.
Skorchas are unreliable devices capable of spraying burning Promethium over an area where any unfortunate victim will be reduced to burning remains in seconds.
A Waaagh is born when a single Warboss manages to organize a massive number of Orks and lead them to fight and conquer. They are often so large that they can raze planetary systems.
Orks dislike the lack of fighting to the point they will start seeking a bigger, meaner enemy right after the end of a battle.
A way to stop an Ork from fighting might be to move all enemies out of his reach, but so far it hasn't been successfully tested given the rates of in-fighting among Orks.
Wearing an Irongob means that the wearer is a mighty warlord indeed. Many outside Ork society don't know this, but a headbutt from the wearer will be enough to teach them.
Stormboyz jump attacks are completely unpredictable. Their Rokkit Packs allow them to raze the battlefield efficiently but are also prone to misfiring and landing failures.
Roks are hollowed-out asteroids fitted with guns, engines, and packed full of Orks itching for a fight. They can drop troops straight into battle, blasting anything that gets in the way.
A Deff Dread embodies the main ideals of Ork warfare: they're big, shooty and stompy. These combat walkers bring enough firepower to tip the scales of any battle in the Orks' favour.
Gorkanauts are built with the sole purpose of being "proper killy". Equipped with a Deffstorm Mega-Shoota and the massive Klaw of Gork, they are incredibly fearsome in battle.
Coming in all shapes and sizes, the clanking walkers and vehicles of the Orks are designed with one common purpose in mind: to shoot, chop and krump any git in their way.
Ork encampments are often hard to differentiate from actual battlefields. There are countless accounts of Orks charging out of strongholds that are hidden in plain sight.
Grukk's might and ambition pushed him to leave his planet to fight and conquer whole systems. By the time he arrived at Sanctus Reach, his Waaagh was counted in billions.
Crazed Orks belonging to Kults of Speed favour warbikes. These deafening contraptions can be seen approaching in clouds of black exhaust smoke, their riders grinning maniacally.
Not wanting to be left out of the WAAAGH!, gretchin construct these small tanks to mimic their bigger Ork brethren. However, the tiny tanks have a tendency to explode.
Orky-tech defies the laws of physics, but some Orks, called Spannerz, seem to have an affinity for it nonetheless. These Orks will tinker with the ‘worky bitz’ to improve it.
A charging mob of Orks is often preceded by a vast cloud of black smoke from all the exhausts and overheating weaponry. This can help to hide their advance.
Gretchin may be small and individually weak, but get enough of them in one place and they can be a force to be reckoned with, striking at an enemy from all angles.
Ork battlecries may seem absurd to the casual listener, but they seem to work. The amount of shouting seems to compel them all to fight even harder.
Gork is the more brutally kunnin’ (or is it kunningly brutal?) of the two Ork deities, and entreating his name grants some of his strength to nearby Orks.
The rank and file of Ork armies, tides of Boyz crash against enemy forces as a green tide of howling violence, armed with sluggas and choppas that are as crude as they are deadly.
What's faster than a Warbuggy, killier than a Warbike and flies through the air like a bird? Orks don't know, so they attach rotors and rokkits to scavenged Warbikes and pilot them into battle.
Bigger and meaner than regular orks, Nobz act as sergeant-at-arms, champions, oppressors and role models. They tend to lead by example, plunging head-first into the thick of battle.
With the roar of engines and the crackle of flames, Snazzwagon drivers race each other to the front lines on these lightly-built speedsters, howling as they create a devastating inferno.
Orks can become addicted to the intense kickback and explosive sounds of firearms. Those fondest of these sensations will devote their time to finding reasons to pull the trigger again.
Tankbustas enter the battlefield with a primal desire to hunt down armoured vehicles, scavenging the greatest trophies from their prey to brag of their felled quarries.
Once, Rukkatrukk Squigbuggies were used to feed Squigs to Speed Freeks on the move. It was only after a rabid Attack Squig was accidentally launched that its true potential was realised.
These specialists prefer to rely on "kunnin' trikz" rather than fighting the opponent head-on. Kommandos are distrusted by most other Greenskins, who find their methods distinctly "un-Orky".
Sometimes, a Battlewagon bears so much weaponry it becomes a Gunwagon. These piloted beasts ravage enemy lines until an unlucky shot to its ammunition depots makes them explode spectacularly.
Flames and the resulting sizzle of scorched enemies have an undeniable appeal to the Orks. Greenskins with functioning Burnas will go great lengths to reduce anything to cinders.
Ork medicine is not an exacting kind of science, and often seems to do more harm than good. However, treated Orks have been known to get up and fight after the most severe injuries.
From all the ways Orks could worship their gods Gork and Mork, it's very convenient that the main method to show devotion to Gork just happens to be more fighting.
It's theorized that Ork tech is somehow warp-infused, as it only seems to work because the Orks believe it should. That would explain why Ork weapons are useless to anyone else.
Ork mechanical repairs tend to consist of nothing but a Mekboy hitting it hard with a hammer. Somehow, this seems to work.
Eternal fanatics of the crushin' and krumpin', Orks often outfit vehicles with a giant spiked ball on a chain that they swing in battle against enemy tanks and structures.
As far as Orks are concerned, there is no such thing as too much dakka. If there’s the slightest amount of space left on a vehicle, then it clearly needs more guns!
Orks like nothing more than fighting, and the rallying cry of WAAAAGH! draws them to battle from far and wide.
Every Ork knows that Ghazghkull Mag Uruk Thraka is the greatest warboss ever! Just being in his presence inspires the boyz to fight as hard as they can.
Don’t make Zagstruk mad! He’ll leap into the air on his bionic legs and make ready to plunge onto his target in a devastating attack.
Famed Captain of the 4th Company. He has oftentimes defied the Codex Astartes, making use of tactics that clashed with Guilliman's teachings.
Chief Librarian of the Ultramarines chapter. He possesses the unique psychic ability to foresee events before they come to pass and uses these visions to guide his brothers to victory.
Marneus Calgar is the Chapter Master of the Ultramarines. He was the first known Space Marine to go through the Rubicon Primaris to become a Primaris Space Marine.
Infiltrator squads are among the most numerous and versatile of the Space Marines, capable of both disrupting key enemy targets and defending strategical positions.
The Firstborn squads of Tactical Marines are heavily trained in the use of a myriad of weapons to quickly adapt to any situation in battle.
Squads of Assault Intercessors swiftly charge into battle and slay their enemies with a combination of ranged and brutal close-quarter strikes.
Reivers are elite assault specialists with special training and wargear for rapid insertion and lightning-fast strikes. They can sow turmoil before the enemy even knows they are there.
Primaris Intercessor Squads are the mainstay of the new breed of Space Marines, capable of brutal firepower without compromising on their predecessor's versatility.
After the atrocities that the tyranids commited on Macragge, the Ultramarines forged the first squads specialised in battling bio-horrors.
Inceptors use their speed and bulk to spearhead Space Marine attacks. Their immense firepower is enough to leave the enemy open to an attack by follow-up waves of Space Marines.
These heavy support squads are armed with Plasma Incinerators, perfect for providing covering fire and powerful enough to annihilate enemies caught in the Hellblaster's sight.
Space Marines on bikes can attack at phenomenal speeds, using surprise and momentum to overwhelm their enemies.
As the most gifted tank commander of the Ultramarines, Antaro Chronus became the first Marine to bear the title of "Spear of Macragge" since the times of the Great Crusade.
Leading from the front with crozius in hand, the chaplain’s role is to inspire faith and fury in those fighting alongside him, as well as to perform the sacred rituals of the chapter.
Serving with Chaplain Kastor, Polixis was instrumental in saving planet Atari from suffering a horrible fate after it was overrun by a chaos cult uprising.
Sergeant Allectius fought to protect Cassothea from a massive Necron attack. When his superior fell in battle, Allectius assumed Company command for the rest of the gruelling campaign.
A recent improvement of anti-gravitic technology in the Imperium gave way to the Impulsor, a fast-moving assault tank capable of deploying a Primaris squad into the heart of battle.
Ancients are unshakable warriors from a Chapter's Honour Guard who are sworn to carry the Chapter's Standard forward, not dishonour or lose it, and protect it with their lives.
The Gravis power armour of Aggressor Marines is customised with a shoulder-mounted grenade launcher to increase their ability to deliver cover fire and contest rough terrain.
Unmatched veteran marksman and instructor. No less than four Ultramarines Captains attribute their success to the teachings of Torias Telion.
Judiciars are the embodiment of the Chapter Master's will in the battlefield, in charge of keeping Space Marines in line and quieting any sign of disobedience.
Fast, aggressive and hard-hitting, a perfectly coordinated assault from an Inceptor Squad could break the lines of even the most resilient foes.
These expert and methodical warriors enter the battlefield in richly ornamented panoplies, bearing Storm Shields capable of withstanding the most destructive strikes.
Veteran of the Indomitus Crusade, Lucian Calsius has proved himself time and again despite being a relative newcomer to the Chapter.
Battle-brothers who train as Devastator Centurions must endure additional intense training just to learn to handle the immense recoil of their weaponry.
Not all battles can be fought with bolter and chainsword. When it comes to matters of the warp, Ultramarine Librarians are trained in countless techniques, both offensive and defensive.
Their mighty armour allows them to advance through difficult terrain with ease. Instead of heavy guns, they wield Siege Drills capable of shattering buildings and armoured vehicles.
The largest Dreadnought model ever deployed in battle. Mortally wounded Primaris Marines are interred into these machines and given another chance to serve the Emperor.
The lauded Cato Sicarius is one of the greatest heroes of the Ultramarines. He's been known to perform great feats and has snatched victory from the jaws of defeat on many occasions.
This main battle tank provides armoured support to the units on the ground. It uses anti-gravitic technology developed by Belisarius Cawl.
Guided by the principles of the Codex Astartes, the Ultramarines are the most disciplined and cohesive fighting force in the Imperium.
The Codex Astartes has much to say about the perils of an exhausted fighting force. To hold back and recover today means to prevail tomorrow.
Not all battles can be won on the ground alone. Sometimes it is better to step back and unleash devastation in the form of flaming holy promethium.
Calling in the support of these distinctive gunships can swiftly turn the tide of battle in the Ultramarines’ favour.
Capable of swiftly learning from the actions of their enemies, the Ultramarines can turn any attack on their own into a devastating counterassault.
The Ultramarines have long memories, and no slight will ever go unpunished. Should an Ultramarine fall in battle, his brothers will not rest until vengeance is done.
New recruits to the Ultramarines start off as lightly armoured scouts to prove their worth. Despite their junior status, they provide a vital function to the chapter’s operations.
Space Marine Eliminators are expert marksmen who stalk the highest value targets across the battlefield and eliminate them with well-placed sniper shots.
These veteran Space Marines serve as the Chapter Master’s personal retinue and are charged with protecting him and carrying his standard into battle.
This title is bestowed upon the Ultramarines’ foremost tank commander. He reports directly to the Chapter Master and is an advisor in all matters to do with heavy armour.
Whether by their adherence to the Codex Astartes or their ability to adapt to any situation, it is undeniable the Ultramarines have achieved many victories and defied impossible odds.
Since the dawn of time when tribes of proto-humans on Terra battled against one another, mastery of the higher ground has proven to be a key element in ensuring victory.
When it comes to tactical principles, the Ultramarines need look no closer than the Codex Astartes, which contains a wealth of strategic advice for any situation.
Vanguards are elite reconnaissance troops, who can slip behind enemy lines and wreak havoc. They were used to great effect in the Pariah Nexus campaign.
As Captain of the 4th Company, Uriel Ventris is also the Master of the Fleet, responsible for coordinating the Chapter's warship armada when engaging in ship-to-ship combat.
Those with psychic powers are feared throughout the Imperium and for good reason – channelling the warp can open gateways to that realm and bring forth nightmares.
Divining the future is beyond the ability of most psykers. But Varro Tigurius is no ordinary psyker. His visions offer glimpses of the future that can aid his brothers in battle.
The simplest use of the warp is to channel it into destructive energy. This power can take many forms, such as lightning, flame, or sheer telekinetic force.
The warp isn’t just used to destroy. By manipulating the energies of the warp, it’s possible to grant benefits that strengthen and empower oneself and one’s allies in battle.
Marneus Calgar is known for being one of the greatest tacticians in the Imperium, able to predict enemy movements and counter them before they even have a chance to strike.
Bolters are capable of firing self-propelled rounds that explode after hitting the target. Slowly throughout the millennia, the Bolter became a holy symbol of the Emperor's wrath.
The greatest of the Ultramarines are chosen to bear the sacred relics of the chapter, offering a great advantage in battle.
The Ultramarines possess a wealth of heavy armoured support for both the ground and air. These work in unison with the Space Marines on the ground to drive back the enemy.
Even the Codex Astartes cannot deny that getting up close and personal generally yields effective results... at great danger of course.
The strict command hierarchy of the Ultramarines allows them to deploy quickly and efficiently while letting every squad perform their duties to maximum effect.
The Ultramarines take their oaths of brotherhood extremely seriously. If one encounters trouble, others will quickly rally around.
Famed Captain of the 4th Company. He has oftentimes defied the Codex Astartes, making use of tactics that clashed with Guilliman's teachings.
Primarily proficient in the use of ranged weaponry, Sternguard Veterans have a record of making every shot count, and are entrusted with the use of rare specialist ammunition in battle.
Since the times of the Horus Heresy, the Ultramarines have been known for their sturdy leadership, from their Chapter Masters and heroes to their Captains and squad Sergeants.
Following the Ultramarine's taste for adaptability, this highly flexible all-terrain vehicle is able to both open a breach through enemy lines and swiftly engage the enemy's scouting elements.
A Desolation Marine squad can provide long-range support to their battle brothers, carrying heavy weaponry that would prove unwieldy to any that hadn't crossed the Rubicon Primaris.
While the Chapter's battle brothers engage the enemy in the front lines, the Stormtalon Gunship acts as both an interceptor in the skies, and a menace to the enemy's rear lines.
The return of Guilliman in one of the Imperium's darkest hours was, for many, the turning point that pushed them to fight with more zeal than ever to see the Imperium return to its former glory.

The Apothecarion is tasked with the recovery of fallen battle brother gene-seed. The recovered material is taken back to the Chapter, so that it may again be used in the creation of a new battle brother.
The overwhelming force of an Ultramarine attack will rapidly take control of strategic targets and minimize the chances of enemy retaliation.
Spread thin fighting wars across the vast Galaxy, the Chapter Council of the Ultramarines plays an essential role in deploying the optimal resources for each campaign.
Primaris or Firstborn, recruit or Captain, the duty of an Ultramarine to the Chapter and the Imperium only ends with his last breath.
Imotekh is the Phaeron of the Sautekh dynasty, and ruler of dozens of tomb worlds across the galaxy. He is a strategic genius who is constantly looking for ways to expand his empire.
Imotekh’s strategic prowess has been honed over millions of years. He knows exactly where to place himself in battle to do the most damage and reap the greatest rewards.
One of the galaxy’s greatest generals. Zahndrekh is known for abiding to a strict code of conduct in battle – fighting honourably and treating prisoners with respect.
Zahndrekh has been waging constant war on the galaxy for millennia. He has a seemingly endless supply of warriors, such that he never lets up the pressure on his opponent.
A great Cryptek, known for his powers over time itself. He opposed the biotransference process that turned the Necrontyr into undying Necrons, but has since embraced all it has to offer.
Orikan’s mastery over time itself lets him peer into the past and the future alike, and even ‘walk back’ time to correct the mistakes he made earlier.
Often sent into battle in seemingly endless swarms, these small silver beetle-like constructs can break down matter into pure energy for their Necron masters.
These flying constructs use their monomolecular proboscis to inject frenzied units with energy, driving them to even greater madness and destructive potential.
Some Necron warriors fall victim to a curse of madness that leaves them craving flesh and blood. Draped in the skins of their enemies, they are a terrifying sight to behold.
These Necron warriors carry Gauss Flayers – weapons that shoot a bright green flash of molecular disassembling energy. An enemy is reduced to its constituent atoms in seconds.
The standard infantry troop for the Necrons. The great Sautekh Overlords were only able to conquer countless planets thanks to these soulless automata following their every order.
Immortals are powerful Necrons, still able to think and act with basic sentience. Often armed with Tesla Carbines, they fire living energy that arcs from one enemy to another.
The wraith is a stealthy construct able to phase in and out of space-time thanks to its Phase Shifter device. This allows it to scout the battlefield and report back to its masters.
Each Immortal carries a spark of the living being they once were – now all they sense is the thrill of the kill and the satisfaction of obeying their masters.
Destroyers are Necrons cursed with an uncontrollable urge to destroy all life. Ophydian destroyers are able to burrow into pocket dimensions and re-emerge to ambush their prey.
Praetorians serve as enforcers of ancient Necrontyr law. Usually a rare sight in battle, the rediscovery of many Tomb Worlds by the Sautekh kept them in the dynasty's front lines.
Technomancers are a specialised type of Cryptek, able to repair Necron troops and canoptek constructs in the midst of battle.
An airborne unit known for its versatility, fast speed and erratic movement. A swarm of tomb blades can quickly overwhelm even the toughest defences.
Large anti-gravitic constructs shaped like arachnids. They cruise the battlefield conducting repairs on Necron systems, while their large bodies create and deploy canoptek scarabs.
Equipped with fierce short-range weaponry, Cryptothralls keep threats out of their master's way, allowing them to carry out their masterful plans without interference.
Deathmarks are assassins and snipers that can phase in an out of space-time at will in order to ambush their prey. Very few enemies who have met one ever live to tell the tale.
This modified version of the Doom Scythe is often used as a troop transport. As well as attacking with its Tesla weaponry, it can drop Necron troops to the heart of battle.
The Psychomancer is a specialised Cryptek able to create illusions and hard-light constructs in order to unleash an enemy’s worst fears against them.
Shockingly fast and nimble for their size, few enemies can withstand the overwhelming flurry of attacks that these Destroyers can unleash with their Hyperphase weaponry.
Necron warriors inevitably rise back up to fight again, but the process can take some time. This construct speeds up the reanimation process with a beam of repairing nano-scarabs.
Specialised Crypteks with power over time itself. They can speed it up or slow it down to suit the battle, aiding their allies or hindering their opponents as needed.
This distinctive attack aircraft is capable of operating both in the void and within planetary atmospheres. The sound of it approaching is known to instil terror in its enemies.
This destroyer has mounted itself onto a repulsor chassis, and bound its limbs into heavy gauss cannons, ideal for obliterating all living beings from afar.
Elite protectors and emissaries of the nobility. They were granted the highest quality necrodermis, making them extremely hard to damage. They plough into battle with their warscythes.
This mobile weapons platform is slow-moving but brings doom to all enemies. It is loaded with powerful Tesla weaponry, and once in range, it shows the true meaning of annihilation.
The superior targeting systems of Hexmark Destroyers enables them to easily unleash volleys of death with their six Disintegrator Pistols, quickly turning any living organisms into dust.
These specialized Crypteks wield plasmic lances that can make even the air scream in agony. The living lightning that they wield makes short work of any enemy that gets too close.
Individually, Necron scarabs are weak and easily dealt with, but in large numbers, they can pose a serious threat to even the most hardened enemy.
Once, these skeletal vehicles dragged unwilling Necrontyr to the furnaces for bio-transference. Now, they trawl the battlefield for damaged Necrons, ready to return them to the fight.
Necron Lords of the Sautekh Dynasty are counted among the most aggressive and eager in attempting a new wave of expansion to restore the Necrons to their former glory.
Fearsome hexapedal walkers, equipped with powerful weaponry and usually deployed against enemy tanks and armour. Their precision targeting relay can also provide data to allied units.
A huge construct fitted with a devastating doomsday blaster. Doomstalkers are often used as sentries to protect Necron overlords and their treasures.
Even the greatest Sautekh can succumb to the destroyer curse. These towering Skorpekhs efficiently butcher enemy lines while commanding the frenzied in brief moments of clarity.
Obyron is the bodyguard of Nemesor Zahndrekh and accompanies his master on all campaigns. He is the main reason why Zahndrekh has managed to survive this long.
A massive mobile fortress, it serves both as a formidable assault platform and as a symbol of Necron dominance. Many have fled in terror after seeing a monolith rise over the battlefield.
Only the most strong-willed of the nobility were chosen to become Overlords, retaining their sentience and individuality through the biotransference process.
Even a Necron that has been shattered into its component parts can reform. The living necrodermis pulls limbs back together so that the warrior can serve its overlord once more.
Mounted atop a monolith, this giant weapon emits a stream of anti-matter particles that detonate on contact with other matter.
The legions of the Sautekh Dynasty excel in systematic extermination, concentrating their fire upon a target until it's completely obliterated.
Every other species that encounters the Necrons soon learns that they are incredibly hard to kill. Necron warriors can arise back into the fray after sustaining the most grievous of injury.
Necrons are extremely durable in battle. Even great enemy battalions will lose all hope when they see their numbers dwindle while the Necron host remains mostly unchanged.
Endless are the tales of Necron shattered bodies reforming on the battlefield. Witchfire flaring back to life in their dead eye-lenses confirms a Necron has not yet been bested.
The Sautekh dynasty is determined to retake their ancient domain and will not let anything get in their way. Even the most hardened defenders are pushed back by the endless tide.
Many Necron weapons are equipped with pulsing orbs, charged to the brim with eldritch energies. When activated, they can unleash an amount of power equivalent to a solar flare.
Some Necron Overlords bind disruption fields into their weapons, allowing them to shred even the heaviest of tank armour without difficulty.
Necron commanders have had millions of years to master the art of tactics and strategy, and they are rarely left surprised.
Canoptek Spyders shouldn't be understimated. Their fabricator function is so optimized that an unchecked group of them could overwhelm a whole army by creating an endless tide of Scarabs.
Necron Overlords are inherently vindictive. If you destroy something belonging to them, they will hold nothing back in their vengeance.
Necrons can overcharge the molecular disintegration emitters in their weapons to flay away additional layers of enemy armour in explosive eruptions of glowing dust.
This powerful artifact pulses with energy that supercharges Necron self-repair systems and is able to bring entire legions back into fighting conditions.
By phasing through their dimensional corridors, Necron units can appear anywhere on the battlefield.
The sound of incoming Doom Scythes and Night Scythes is known to terrify the enemy, even before the aircraft unleash their devastating payload.
Canoptek Scarabs are equipped with self-destruction protocols, that cause them to explode in a hail of razor-sharp fragments.
All Necron troops obey their overlord without question. At the overlord’s command, they will stop what they are doing and unleash their weapons in perfect synchronicity.
When a Necron is slain, its crawling limbs reattach, its sundered torso reforms, and the Necron rises again. There is no rest for Necrons who fall in the service of their master.
Not all Necron overlords command from the rear. Many like to take to the battlefield themselves to personally unleash carnage upon their enemies.
Necron overlords are not known to retreat. The many victories achieved over millions of years honed their pride to the point of being disgusted by the mere idea of falling back.
There is no escaping the wrath of the Sautekh Dynasty. Planet after planet have fallen against magnificent displays of meticulous annihilation.
Necron Tomb Worlds are scattered across the entire galaxy. Each one contains millions of dormant Necrons, ready to awaken and unleash war upon anyone who stumbles upon them.
Every Necron overlord knows that it is their destiny to rule over the entirety of creation, and absolutely nothing will stop them from pursuing this goal.
Royal Wardens exist to ensure the will of their Overlord is carried out by the Dynasty's armies, but they possess enough initiative and command to adapt these plans in the midst of battle.
After Horus' death, Abaddon formed the Black Legion and took on the title of Warmaster, determined to overcome Horus' failure and become the one to bring down the False Emperor.
At the end of the Horus Heresy, Chaos Space Marines from all legions came together under Abaddon’s banner to join the Black Crusade against the Imperium.
Known as the Herald of the Apocalypse, Haarken Worldclaimer’s job is to proclaim the coming of Abaddon’s forces in order to spread fear and confusion among enemies.
Haarken’s Helspear is a daemon-touched weapon that incites its bearer into ever greater fury every time it is plunged into a victim.
A former Word Bearer, Sylar cast off his original colours and joined Abaddon as a sorcerer. Both a gift and a curse, his formidable command of the warp came at a cost to his sanity.
A sorcerer reaches into the warp without regard. This yields powerful and devastating results but corruption and insanity constantly pick away at the sorcerer’s soul.
Sylar's mastery of the Warp is such that he can make it flow through his warriors, bestowing upon them the blessings of the Gods and increasing their effectiveness in battle.
Powerful Sorcerers can channel streams of unholy power through their eyes, charring and melting anything caught in their view.
The energies of Chaos can be manipulated to course through the body, swelling the frame with the strength to tear a tank in two.
Chaos spawn are mindless mutants who have been twisted into monsters by Chaos and lost all sense of sentience and sanity. All that’s left is the urge to kill.
The Black Legion recruits Chaos Space Marines from other legions, chapters and warbands. Upon joining the Black Legion, these recruits repaint their armour to black and gold.
Whether they hail from the days of the Horus Heresy or have turned recently, the combination of their gene-given gifts with blessings of the dark Gods makes them an enemy to fear.
Remnants of an ancient Thousand Sons ritual, these marines appear to be nothing but ancient dust within suits of power armour. Ominous and silent, they are obedient automatons.
Empowered by the Blood God, berserkers charge into battle with little regard for personal safety. Their only desire is to shed as much blood as possible.
Within the Black Legion, the followers of Slaanesh seek pain to fulfil their desires. Noise Marines do this by using sonic weaponry to fell their enemies with an unbearable shriek.
These Chaos Space Marines have given up all semblance of humanity and are entirely possessed by daemons. They feel no pain, and their bodies can mutate and warp.
When a Chaos Space Marine devotes himself to Nurgle, his body is blessed by the Grandfather to fester and bloat with disease and decay.
A Chaos Space Marine faces many threats, from dying in battle to succumbing to corruption and madness. Few ever survive to become veterans.
Sometimes a warrior captures the interest of the Ruinous Powers. Champions of the Black Legion will do whatever it takes to earn the favour of the whole ruinous pantheon.
The Chosen are power-hungry veterans of the Chaos Space Marine warbands, known to undertake the most destructive and dangerous missions for the glory of Chaos.
Weapons infused with the power of daemons are truly fearsome to face in battle. They can cut straight through the thickest armour and empower the wielder in the process.
Blessed by Khorne, the Master of Executions stalks the battlefield looking for enemy champions and commanders to decapitate. Every trophy taken is savoured.
When a Chaos Space Marine wishes to offer himself up completely to the Gods, he must spend months preparing his body with rituals and ceremonies.
Moving undetected through the warp, these Chaos Space Marines can slide into reality to ambush their targets at will and then disappear again just as quickly.
Transformed by the blessings of Nurgle, this formation of Black Legionaries wreaks ruin upon their enemies with toxic weaponry that renders them unable to defend themselves.
Specialised warriors in exceptionally heavy armour. In battle, they relentlessly advance towards enemy lines discharging deadly volleys while protected by their ironclad panoplies.
A member of a hedonistic Chaos Space Marine formation devoted to Slaanesh. They swore allegiance to Abaddon, for he grants them endless opportunities to create anguish and torment.
The Hounds of Abaddon is a group of elite Khorne Berzerkers within the Black Legion. They plunge into battle with enraged fervour to take the enemy's skulls for the Skull Throne.
These specialized psykers are able to channel daemons into living hosts even in the midst of battle, binding both of them together to create a Possessed Space Marine.
Chaos Sorcerers call upon the warp to devastate their opponents. The constant exposure to the Immaterium quickly takes its toll, and most sorcerers end up insane.
The Chosen are already elite veterans of the Black Legion. Any among them to gain additional recognition as a champion is a formidable warrior indeed.
A former Chaplain who has embraced Chaos. Dark Apostles live in the hope of someday being chosen for possession by powerful daemons.
An Obliterator is a former techmarine who has been corrupted to become a mutant hybrid of man, machine and daemon.
These terrifying Daemon Engines butcher their prey with cannons, claws and tendrils. They are often seen sprawling war zones in search of bodies to tear and souls to consume.
A critically injured warrior can be entombed inside the bulk of a Helbrute to continue the fight for Chaos. Most consider this a terrible fate, a mockery by the gods.
Over ten thousand years, some warriors have gained status and respect to be considered champions among their kind. In battle, other legionaries will rally around them.
The most powerful champions of Chaos are elevated to high standing and granted additional blessings. They serve as commanders on the battlefield.
This bestial daemon engine charges towards its foes to rip them to pieces in close combat. They can tear even the heaviest armour to pieces with their claws.
A powerful sorcerer who was once a member of the Thousand Sons. His mastery of the warp is such that he once brought Magnus the Red, his former master, to his knees.
Known as the Arch-Lord Discordant, he emits an aura of scrapcode that quickly corrupts all machine spirits nearby, sowing confusion and chaos in enemies.
To the warriors of the Black Legion, being possessed by a daemon is a great honour, and the means to even greater power.
All warriors of the Black Legion vie to be noticed by Abaddon, for gaining the Warmaster’s favour is the fastest route to power and status.
Dark Apostles offer up prayers to the Gods to direct their attention to their corrupted followers. If they are deemed worthy, the Gods will bestow a mote of their power onto them.
Mutations are but the favour of the Dark Gods made manifest. These blessings aid warriors chosen by the Gods to outlive constant battles, and further spread the influence of Chaos.
Many Chaos Marines believe that they were betrayed by the Emperor during the Horus Heresy, not the other way around. They have spent millennia planning revenge.
Daemonic possession makes a warrior far stronger and tougher in battle… all for the small price of one’s soul.
Its bitter hatred towards the Emperor and its thirst for revenge against the Imperium pushes the Black Legion ever further. They will not rest until Terra goes up in flames.
Khorne rallies his followers to ever greater levels of frenzy, bestowing great strength in combat in exchange for madness and fanaticism.
Chaos Space Marines will often enter into pacts with daemons, offering their service in exchange for power and glory.
To court the gaze of the Chaos Gods is to risk their whims. The champions of chaos who cannot bear the gifts of the gods now exist only as mindless aberrations.
The four Chaos Gods bestow gifts upon their followers in the form of marks and powerful mutations that the Black Legion wields in battle to further spread the domain of Chaos.
Those sworn to spread the corruption of Nurgle become vectors of decay, horrifically resilient as their master's blessings makes their rotting brains inured to bodily pain.
Tzeentch is always manipulating the fates, tugging at strands in inscrutably subtle ways to change the course of history.
Those devoted to Slaanesh throw themselves into battle to feed on the pain that surrounds them, channelling all these deadly delights to enter a frenzy of gore and pain.
Chaos Space Marines thrive on cruelty and ruthlessness and will never show mercy. Putting the weak out of their misery is standard practice.
After the Horus Heresy, the exiles were banished to the warp storm known as the Eye of Terror. For ten thousand years they fought and planned their revenge.
It’s possible to call upon the Dark Gods for assistance during battle. The Gods are fickle and may not respond, but when they do, the effects are devastating.
Heldrakes are winged daemon engines that swoop across the battlefield and plunge down on enemy aircraft, ripping them to shreds to dominate the sky.
A powerful daemon bound into the sword of the same name that is wielded by Abaddon the Despoiler. It can rend even reality apart.
Over the course of the millennia following the Horus Heresy, Abaddon has commanded the forces of Chaos in large-scale attacks against the Imperium known as Black Crusades.
Warbands of the Black Legion are known to be diverse and adaptable, but something proves true across them all: those in commanding positions have been blessed by the Gods of Chaos.
Not even the temporary loss of his arms stopped this warrior from fighting. Originally one of Angron's World Eaters, he found a new purpose after joining Abaddon and his Black Legion.
The tendrils of Chaos spread far and wide, and have influenced millions across through the millennia. Dark Disciples traverse the Galaxy, seeking more adepts to join the fight against the Imperium.
Havocs bring heavy firepower to the lines of the Black Legion, wielding weaponry so powerful they often see themselves as gods, eliminating targets with each twitch of the finger.
Its not uncommon for a Chaos Marine to be possessed by a Daemon. Once these murderous denizens of the Warp take over, the Marine's thoughts and actions are no longer his alone.
His mastery of predictions and ability to peer into the past and future has allowed the Saim-Hann to fight for the times ahead with hope and determination.
Expert jetbike rider, Eliac Zephyrblade is known for leading entire warhosts in perfectly orchestrated assaults to reclaim planets previously inhabited by the Aeldari.
A warden of the Saim-Hann, Ghaelyn has fulfilled her duties time and again leading counteroffensives against any foe who dared attack an Aeldari sanctuary.
All Aeldari are trained for battle at some point in their lives, and all will don the war mask wilfully in times of war to protect their Craftworld.
Many Storm Guardians once served Aspect Shrines dedicated to close combat. When necessity calls, they will once more use the deadly skills they once honed to perfection.
Aeldari Rangers follow the Path of the Outcast. Many still serve their craftworld by seeking out potential threats and trying to locate lost Maiden Worlds to create new sanctuaries.
So few are the Aeldari that all are battle-trained and part of a Guardian Host. Saim-Hann Guardians are also trained in jetbike combat, but are yet to earn the right to ride into battle.
Combining their psychic abilities and military experience, Warlock cast runes of battle to bolster the guardian hosts at their command and eliminate threats to the Craftworld.
Saim-Hann Windriders expertly handle their jetbikes at astounding speeds and impossible angles. They have been known to defeat enemies before they even hear the sound of the engines.
These Raptor jetbikes are ridden into battle by a pair of Aeldari rangers. Accustomed to firing at high speeds, the pillion rider harasses enemy forces with pinpoint sniper accuracy.
The deadliest of the close combat squads deployed by the Aeldari. These excellent infiltrators stalk their prey through the shadows before falling upon them with the wrath of Khaine.
In Aeldari Mythology, the hawk is a symbol of retribution. These aerial troops pay homage to their mythological homonym by dealing swift death to their enemies from the skies.
Warp Spiders epitomise the doctrine of aggressive defence. Using an arcane dimensional device, they teleport in the blink of an eye and strike without warning from unseen quarters.
The body and weapons of Ghost Warriors like the Wraithblade are powered by a spirit stone, allowing the dead to control these constructs and fight for the Craftworld again.
Specialized in close combat, they use precision and agility to efficiently slay their prey. Their piercing war cry is amplified into a mind-wreaking shock wave by their masks.
Nuadhu is possibly the most skilled and rash rider in existence. A legend among the Wild Riders of the Saim-Hann, he's often seen commanding impossible strike and fade charges.
Death doesn't grant respite from war to the Aeldari. Spiritseers can bring Ghost warriors to life by using a spirit stone, which contains the soul of a departed Aeldari.
One of the mainstays of Saim-Hann armies, Vypers are highly mobile weapon platforms, capable of laying enemies down with intense and precise firepower.
Witchblades not only enhance a Warlock's psychic abilities but can also be used as conduits for the wielder's powers and turn them into terrifying opponents at close quarters.
The most common Aeldari ghost warriors. Wraithguard are impervious to damage and enter battle armed with terrifying weapons able to open momentary rifts between the warp and realspace.
Crimson Hunters are trained to become exceptional pilots and marksmen, to the point that even the most complex and deadly manoeuvres come naturally to them.
No Aspect Warrior revels more in destruction than the Fire Dragons. When deployed straight into the heart of battle using a vehicle, they can cause immense disarray to enemy lines.
Striking Scorpions are merciless killers without exception. Their ability to become one with the shadows has turned many battles around against unsuspecting enemies.
Few dare speak the true name of Wraithblades for fear of inciting the wrath of Khaine, the Aeldari god associated with murder, violence and war.
Spurring their allies as they wreak havoc through enemy lines, these battle-psykers are vital in performing the sudden assault strategies of the Saim-Hann.
Lightly armoured but heavily armed, the War Walkers serve as scouts and mobile heavy support in rough terrain. The formidable power of their weapons can take whole enemy squads at once.
The Falcon is a fast, mobile and hard-hitting Grav-tank. This versatile vehicle is driven only by veteran pilots who wholly exploit its flight capability to rain death upon the enemy.
Boasting an unmatched attunement with the spirits of the Saim-Hann, Qelenaris has led countless departed Aeldari back into battle, ready to fulfil their duties as they did in life.
Based on the Falcon's design, the Wave Serpent acts as a specialized troop transport in battle, bringing whole squads of Guardians to the heart of battle.
Fire Prisms are the dedicated tank-hunters of the Saim-Hann. They are armed with a Prism Cannon, a powerful weapon capable of felling a Necron Monolith with a single shot.
No defence can withstand a Saim-Hann strike. Winged Autarchs put their enemies in impossible situations commanding Aeldari Warhosts from a vantage position.
Only former great heroes of the Saim-Hann pilot their statuesque Wraithlords. In battle, these towering warrior-nobles fight in much the same manner as they once did in life.
This sinister aircraft harbours multiple essences of deceased Aeldari who act as co-pilots. Only the most determined Spiritseers can fly them and interact with the departed unscarred
Huge and all-powerful, the Avatar is a god incarnate, the embodiment of the Aeldari deity Khaine and a deadly opponent even for the mightiest powers in the Galaxy.
