Few foes can stand up to a Wraithknight's power. Armed with some of the heaviest weaponry of the Aeldari, these ghost warriors can obliterate masses of soldiers in a heartbeat.
In the expert hands of a Saim-Hann pilot, Aeldari vehicles can perform seemingly impossible manoeuvres that would surprise even the most agile foes.
Long ago, the Aeldari mastered travel through the labyrinthine dimension known as the Webway. Traversing the infinite mazes of this dimension, they can enter battle undetected.
When Aeldari seers sense a looming menace, they summon the certainty and confidence of ancient days into all near them. Doubt and fear are washed away, leaving way to grim resolve.
It's not only the Saim-Hann pilots that should be feared. All Aeldari are trained warriors determined to fight for the Craftworld and capable of assaulting key enemy targets.
These fighters represent the pinnacle of Aeldari aeronautic prowess. Piloted by Saim-Hann's most expert Crimson Hunters, they clear the skies and bring aerial support like no other.
There once was a time in which the Webway spanned the Galaxy. Those days might be long gone, but Aeldari still make use of these dimensional gates to traverse the stars.
The agile and perfectly choreographed way of war of the Saim-Hann can wreak havoc to the enemy lines before they even know they're being attacked.
With their ability to travel at high speeds and teleport short distances, anyone who dares take their eyes from the shadows is doomed to fall against the Saim-Hann.
Like the bloody spear of Khaine, the Wild Rider clans strike from above, their riders and pilots screaming war cries into the raging winds.
Sometimes referred to as the shriek-that-kills, the chilling scream of the Howling Banshees inflicts severe damage to the nervous systems of their foes.
There is no safe refuge against Saim-Hann airborne strikes. Their preternatural ability in the skies is only matched by the precision of their weaponry even at high speeds.
All Aeldari are trained in the handling of shuriken weaponry. The Bladestorm is a commonly used tactic, in which they lay down a hail of continuous fire with pinpoint accuracy.
In Aeldari myth, the Serpent is believed to know all secrets, past and present. In their language, the word for Serpent and secret knowledge is the same: "Saim".
Farseers can wield the eldritch energies as a weapon and are able to will vast psychic storms into existence, powerful enough to injure even heavily armoured enemies.
Saim-Hann's greatly skilled pilots exploit their vehicle's exceptional speed to seemingly vanish from the battlefield, returning moments later to deal death once again.
Infinity Circuits spread throughout all Aeldari Craftworlds. Inside it reside the souls of the departed Aeldari, which act as a massive ancestral mind to guide the living.
The Aeldari are not numerous enough to defend their Craftworlds from every attacker, and are forced to call upon the spirits of the dead to fill their ever-thinning ranks.
Survival alone is not enough - the Aeldari long to see their civilisation restored to its former glory.
When an Avatar of Khaine strikes with this ancient weapon, it can be heard shrieking as it tastes mortal flesh. This is no regular blade, but a manifestation of a dark and sinister god.
The advanced gravity-defying technology on the platforms allows the Eldar to rapidly and effortlessly move heavy weapons across the field of battle regardless of terrain.
Patient and methodical aspect warriors, Dire Avenger's Shuriken Catapults are equipped with an advanced targeter that allows them to unleash a flurry of shurikens with pinpoint precision.
Exarchs at front of Dire Avengers have an uncanny ability to read the ebb and flow of battle, leading their squads with tactics designed to deny attacks of opportunity from opponents.
More aggressive and daring than their kindred, the fighting passion and spirit of the Saim-Hann Craftworld is often reminiscent of Khaine's hunger for battle.
The anti-gravitic motors of Shining Spears’ gleaming jetbikes allow them to skim over the roughest terrains weaving through dense jungles and crumbling architecture without slowing.
Shining Spear Exarchs possess preternatural reflexes and a deep understanding of their jetbikes dynamics, steering confidently at high speeds even with their eyes shut tight.
The Hornet is a small attack craft deployed for reconnaissance and raid missions, speeding ahead of the main force to harry priority targets and strike before the enemy can respond.
The Night Spinner's doomweaver spins deadly monofilament wire into a lethal web launched into the air, ensuring a horrific fate to any foe caught in its descent.
Speed, grace and overwhelming force are the hallmarks of the Howling Banshees. Their Exarchs exhibit the greatest ability of all, enhancing the deadly prowess of their followers.
The Aeldari believe that the spirit of someone murdered passes into a hawk. Swooping Hawks take their name from these wild hunting birds, for they are synonymous with vengeance.
Inhabited by those known as the Asuryani, the craftworlds are continentsized interstellar fortresses, each one representing a small preserved fragment of Aeldari civilisation
Those who try to match blades with a Howling Banshee find their deadliest blows meeting nothing but air, as their foe dances around them before delivering the fatal strike.
The Triskele's unique design lets Howling Banshee Exarchs use this deadly power weapon in close quarters or as a thrown weapon, slicing enemies before returning to their grasp.
Jain Zar has led hundreds of Howling Banshees to war. Furthermore, no other Phoenix Lord has championed the growing cause of the Ynnari more than her.
Having perfected the deadly arts of the aspect shrine of the Howling Banshee for centuries, Autarch Yrlla now brings swift death to the foes who barely blink in her presence.
It was Jain Zar, the devoted matriarch, who perfected and taught the Scream that Steals. Her own psychosonic barrage is so powerful it can liquefy the brains of her victims.
The Autarchs who tread the Path of Command have already completed other Asuryani paths, and aim to develop higher military skills to eliminate any threat with minimal losses.
Considered the longest and most treacherous path, the Path of the Seer is only trodden by those determined enough to develop their psychic talents for the good of the Craftworld.
Most Aeldari follow the call to war voluntarily at some point in their lives. Those who believe they can rebuild their lost empire with fire and blade traverse the Path of the Warrior.
Destruction made manifest, the most warlike Aeldari who walk the Path of the Seer can bring devastation to their foes using nothing but their minds.
Once awakened from his smouldering throne, the Avatar of Khaine will lead the armies of the Aeldari into battle, inciting its merciless rage into their hearts.
While the enemy attempts to take down their swift, devastating vehicles, the Saim-Hann deploy their forces on land to further pressure the enemy into a difficult position.
Amongst the billions of creatures created by the Hive Mind, the Swarmlord stands above all others, as the conduit through which the Hive Mind's implacable will is enforced.
The highest advancement of the Zoanthrope bioform, these creatures drift through the battlefield using their psychic potential, leeching the very life force of their enemies.
The Tervigon never enters the battlefield alone. This creature hosts a dormant swarm in its abdomen and it's been known to overwhelm its prey by spawning scores of lesser bioforms.
These pack predators can lurk undetected for long periods of time. When they emerge from the shadows, their prey is quickly defeated with a flurry of eviscerating talons.
As the Tyranid ecosystem takes hold, Ripper swarms facilitate the speed at which Tyranids strip a planet of its natural resources.
When these living, floating organisms detonate, they cloud the battlefield and cover enemies in acid, poison and pieces of chitin.
When Hive Fleet Leviathan attacks, Hormagaunts act as shock troops. Numbered in the billions, these hunter-slayer organisms are left to rampage and wear down the prey's defences.
Filled with poisonous gases, these rudimentary organisms are driven instinctively towards the enemy before detonating in a nauseating blast of filth and chitinous shrapnel.
The cunning and agile Termagant is one of the most common bioforms in any Hive Fleet. While not very strong individually, when fighting as a swarm, they can overwhelm nearly any enemy.
Boasting the superior synaptic link of Hive Fleet Leviathan, the Tyranid Warrior is the backbone of many Tyranid invasions, serving as synaptic linchpins within a swarm.
Deep within the lumpen form of the Biovore lie a clutch of Spore Mines. This "living artillery" slowly thumps forward, clouding the battlefield with the mines it nurtures.
Sometimes called a "Hellbat" by Imperial soldiers who faced one in battle, the Gargoyle sows terror and confusion from the skies, wearing down enemy lines from unseen quarters.
Genestealers were the first Tyranid bioform discovered by the Imperium. They are vanguard organisms with a unique reproductive cycle that allows them to easily expand their numbers.
The Pyrovore's whole purpose is to sate the Hive's hunger. It's common to see them feeding on the dead while the intelligent bio-weapon on its back fends off approaching enemies.
The whip-like tendrils of a Venomthrope drip with a multitude of alien poisons. The mix of these toxins is so potent that it's believed the touch of a Venomthrope means certain death.
Well armoured and resilient, so extreme is the Tyrant Guard's bio-adaptation that they do not possess any weak spots such as eyes.
Lictors are specialized in infiltration and assassination. Hidden by their chameleonic skin their assaults are clouded and brutal, picking off their enemies one by one.
A Sporocyst embeds itself into the ground like a tick in unprotected skin. From its chitinous shell sprout Spore Mines that pollute the atmosphere to make it ripe for digestion.
Considered the apex of the Tyranid Warrior strain, the presence of a Prime alone can turn a group of Tyranid creatures into an effective and unified fighting force.
Rugged and adaptable organisms, the large frame of the Carnifex allows them to support a great range of weapon grafts, from scything talons to ranged bio-plasma weaponry.
This evolved strain of the Lictor appears to instinctively know how to spread fear through its preys, and uses stealth and assassination to sow dread before the hive attacks.
Hive Guard are spawned to protect Tyranid bio-architecture and vital spore-seeding sites, laying down heavy hails of firepower with their monstrous arsenal of grafted bio-weapons.
Once these burrowing creatures have located prey, they surge upwards in an eruption of soil, talons and claws, swallowing everything above before plunging back under the surface.
Zoanthropes have evolved to harness the psychic might of the Hive Mind. These mobile synapse nodes draw upon the Hive's energies to unleash deadly psychic blasts.
Especially adept in infiltration, Broodlords lead Genestealers from the shadows thanks to their superior synaptic link, which allows them to function independently from the Hive Mind.
The terrifying shriek this creature emits is only surpassed by the deadly blasts of bio-plasma that follow. They are often seen wreaking havoc at the forefront of a Tyranid assault.
Whether by tearing its quarry with its bladed spurs or by shooting its drool cannons with unerring accuracy, the Hive Crone is an aerial menace even to the most skilled pilots.
Tyrannocytes are ejected from orbit, carrying smaller Tyranid bioforms. The impact of planetfall disgorges the creatures that dwell inside, deploying the brooding hosts into battle.
During Tyranid invasions, Harpies can be seen conquering the skies and dropping salvos of organic munitions such as Spore Mines onto the panicked enemy lines.
Possessing great strategic cunning, these evolved bioforms command the swarm on the Hive Mind's behalf. Where the Hive Tyrants bestride the battlefield, death comes for prey.
This living vessel of the Hive Mind wields colossal synaptic power. Its unbridled psychic potential is such that this creature inadvertently creates a protective field around itself.
The Exocrine's only task is to carry its dorsal cannon into optimal firing position. The cannon is an independent organism, capable of reducing tanks with searing blasts of bio-plasma.
Afflicted by an infinite hunger, the Haruspex is a ferocious beast created to consume biomass at a sickening pace. With its lashing tongue, it can devour entire platoons in moments.
Spawned to enact the Hive Mind's will from the skies, the Winged Hive Tyrant is not only a mighty beast in its own right, but also acts as a mobile synaptic nexus for the Tyranid swarm.
Unyielding in battle as any war engine and carrying the pinnacle of Tyranid bio-weaponry, the massive Tyrannofex exists purely to spread destruction to Leviathan's foes.
Tyranids are not mindless beasts. Their synaptic link and instincts allow these cunning creatures to plan complex ambushes to take out any foe.
Whether soaring through the skies or swarming the battlefield, it is no hardship for Tyranids to apparently fade from the battle to stalk their prey before striking again.
The instinctive hunter-slayer behaviour of the Tyranid swarm only adds to the dangers of facing them in battle, making them terrifying and unpredictable foes.
When the savage instincts of the Hive Mind take over, a surge of adrenaline spreads through the swarm, prompting an innate, primal urge to destroy and consume all in its path.
In an attempt not to waste any precious biomass, most Tyranid organisms have been designed by the Hive Mind to be impervious to damage.
Tyranid strains are highly adaptive. The rapid evolutionary cycle of the Tyranids allows them to continually develop defences against new dangers, sometimes even in the midst of battle.
A Hive Fleet infests planets before an invasion to wear down its defences from the inside. The swarm establishes hidden colonies that reveal themselves once the invasion begins.
The swarms of bio-engineered creatures of Hive Fleet Leviathan are seemingly unending. As long as there is biomass available, the Hive Mind will spawn new warriors to fight and consume.
Usually the first amongst the swarm to assail the prey, flying organisms pick at their foes with a combination of deadly dives and airborne fire.
Most Tyranids are hunters by nature. Their biomorphologies are adapted to seeking and consuming all matter in their paths to sate the Hive Mind's endless hunger.
An impenetrable carapace protects the swarm from danger. Its chitinous material is designed to absorb even the heaviest of impacts, turning Tyranids into unstoppable biohorrors.
The Hive Mind is always learning. Tyranids change and evolve continuously, adapting to new foes and environments, ready to take on the most dangerous foes and consume the direst of clusters.
All matter in a planet must be consumed, even its atmosphere. The noxious vapours exuded by the swarm not only makes the air digestible, but also hinders the enemy ability to fight back.
The Leviathan cannot be stopped. When it seems the swarm has been defeated, Hive Ships send new biohorrors straight into battle from orbit.
Hive Fleet Leviathan's superior synaptic link allows the many strands of Tyranids to work together like an organized fighting group and eliminate enemies with synergistic assaults.
Tyranids have no natural predator. Created specifically for the devouring of all matter, they pose one of the greatest threats to all life in the Galaxy.
Tyranids do not invade for territorial gain, pride or vengeance. Rather, their purpose is to harvest valuable biomass and feed their insatiable hunger.
The largest and most widespread hive fleet to date, Leviathan shows clear signs of having learnt from the fates of other fleets, and remains a threat to life in the galaxy.
Neurogaunts are specialized bioforms that act as mobile and armed relays for the Synapse network. They are hosts to parasitic Neurocytes, that extend the range of Synaptic creatures.
Even when a planet has been saved from the Leviathan tide, there is no opportunity for respite. Any remnant of the Hive Fleet will be enough to bring a world to its doom if left unchecked.
Designed for shock assault and swift pursuit, Raveners track their prey over massive distances, detecting the slightest movement as they pursue them with terrifying speed.
Tyranids can close terrifyingly long distances in a single leap thanks to their specialized anatomy, jumping from one prey to another before they have a chance to react.
Though Tyranid bioforms are often specialized in a task, they all share the same instinct for the hunt. Hive Fleet Leviathan hungers, and none will stop it from devouring all.
Overriding the instinctive behaviour of the swarm, synaptic creatures lead the numberless hordes of Tyranids against their foes with great tactical acuity.
Tyrannocytes are the backbone of large-scale invasions, serving as one of the main means of Hive Ship-to-surface transportation for the swarm.
The Swarmlord is the herald of the Hive Mind and may be as old as the Tyranid race itself. This creature preys on empires, and has overseen the extinction of entire civilisations.
Neurothropes can harness the energies syphoned from their foes to both bolster nearby Tyranids and unleash searing psychic blast attacks.
Acting as a living incubator, the Tervigon spawns its dormant broods at will. The new spawn instinctively protect the broodmother, their numbers growing until they overwhelm the enemy.
The Path of the Warrior has many branches, known as Warrior Aspects. Each one reflects a facet of the god Khaine, and boasts its own unique fighting techniques and battlefield role.
The mastery of Webway travel was integral to the survival of the Aeldari. Many of their sanctuaries were saved by reinforcements arriving through this Labyrinthine Dimension.
The Infinity Circuit threaded throughout every Aeldari craftworld can act as a seemingly unlimited vault of ancestral knowledge accrued by the Aeldari through the millennia.
Following the pathways between dimensions is a risk even to the Aeldari. The intricate threads of the Labyrinth Dimension may unveil advantageous secrets, or swallow platoons in its roiling tides.
Aeldari strive to match and surpass the deeds of their ancestry, honing their skills across centuries for the good of the Craftworld and the survival of their kin.
Seeking vengeance on the Imperium, the warriors of the Legions that betrayed the Emperor during the Horus Heresy gathered under Abaddon's banner, bringing the Black Legion into existence.
The heretical symbols found within the Black Legion battleships are far from mere ornaments. Imbued with daemonic energies, they can serve as a bridge between the Dark Gods and their devout servants.
The moods of the Ruinous Powers are fickle and unpredictable. But when wielded correctly, the powers they bestow can be used reliably to bring a gruesome end to invading forces.
The chaotic energies that power the Black Legion's fleets and structures act on the whims of the Ruinous Powers, punishing interlopers and unworthy champions alike.
Warp storms cause unbridled, nightmarish energies to pour into realspace, empowering those capable of manipulating the psychic energies of the Immaterium.
The manifest emotion of battle feeds the Warp, attracting the attention of fearsome daemonic beings who gladly form dark pacts so that the gruesome spectacle may continue.
Gretchin mobs compensate for their lack of warring quality with their sheer quantity. Although feeble-limbed by nature, their bites and stabs can add up to bring down larger opponents.
The orks have showcased time and time again an ability to quickly build a functioning vehicle out of ramshackle parts that would put tech-priests to shame.
Often lit up just for the amusement of seeing things burn, Orks have found ingenious ways to use burning barrels in battle.
Attacking by night is a tried and tested tactic to secure the element of surprise. Beware though, a cunnin' enemy might turn the situation in their favor.
Planning an attack during a dust storm is not an easy task. Even with advanced targeting systems, this ever-changing landscape can hinder a squad's capacity to locate their prey.
The undetermined nature of unexplored alien planets often includes exotic substances in its atmosphere, which have unexpected consequences such as intensified beligerence.
Dormant Necron Obelisks rise when they detect an enemy presence in the skies above a Necron Tomb World. Pulsating with energy, it will seek out the enemy to destroy it with its Tesla Spheres.
There is no respite when fighting the Necrons. With a surge of exotic energies, a recently felled warrior could reappear to exact their revenge on their aggressors.
Millennia of battle have increased the tactical accuity of the Sautekh Dynasty, and taught them how to turn even the most damning of omens to their advantage.
To fight in treacherous geological conditions is a challenge even to the most veteran and agile of warriors, making every step a fight against an unpredictable enemy.
Assaulting during a Solar Storm is a risky endeavour, as they can have unexpected effects, overcharging machinery and filling the air with exotic energies.
Shaping and powering the mysterious living metal requires enormous amounts of power for the Necrons, emanating from their structures and filling the air.
After a Tyranid invasion, all matter on a planet is slowly broken down and digested in pools of biomatter. These are highly valued by the Hive Mind, and will be guarded zealously.
Once the invasion of a planet reaches an advanced state, gruesome structures emerge that protect the precious biomatter until it is entirely consumed by the Hive Fleet.
When Tyranids start consuming a planet, they fill the atmosphere with harmful microscopic spores that allow the hive to eventually consume even the air.
Setting the pools of biomass ablaze before an invasion will send the hive into disarray, but fighting in an active inferno is always a perilous endeavour.
Provoked by the Hive's efforts to consume the atmosphere, this chemical downpour makes even the heaviest armour and chitinous structure unreliable.
The Hive's objective is to consume, and it will resort to any measure to claim the biomatter that it has conquered, even if it means consuming its own spawn.
The vast Imperium is besieged on all corners. To always be ready to defend it, many Imperial Worlds are fully dedicated to stocking up the imperial arsenal with weapons and munitions.
A common sight atop the walls of Ultramarine bases of operations, the Firestrike turret is a flexible defensive weapon ideal for defending the flanks of important structures.
Situational awareness is a key skill in Ultramarine training exercises, leading to good strategical positioning in any terrain, and increased survivability in battle.
Fighting in the midst an Orbital Strike is an hazardous undertaking, though it could well turn the tides of battle in a fortuitous moment.
Battles during a thunderstorm can strain even the most veteran warriors, as the elements impede movement and communication, and interfere with scanning equipment.
The secrecy of a pitch-black environment can prove to be a massive advantage against an unaware enemy, but an incautious assailant might find the dark can hold secrets of its own.
The raging theatres of war intersect with one another in every battle, making them highly unpredictable. Being able to adapt to sudden changes is a key skill to secure victory.
Securing regular support from the orbiting fleet is key to the success of most ground assaults, with the steady influx of troops overwhelming most defensive forces.
A small, psychic Tyranid organism. Neuroloids are most commonly seen beside a Neurotyrant, enhancing its abilities and acting as relays of the creature's synaptic network.
Neurogaunts fulfil a double role on the battlefield. This creature is a relay for the Synapse network and acts as a wall of flesh and claws to protect those who would focus it.
The Barbgaunt has little mind of its own. It's bonded to a cerebral parasite that controls its weapon, using the Barbgaunt as a beast of burden.
Preying on psychic lifeforms, a Psychophage's digestive tract is able to metabolise metaphysical matter into psychocorrosive ash, which it projects in blistering torrents.
The Neurotyrant's giant brain focuses the mental powers of the hive, relaying the synapse network to the horde and orchestrating Tyranids to victory.
The expressed will of a Norn Queen made flesh. These towering organisms evolved for the purpose of preying on gifted enemy commanders and abducting prey from defended strongholds.
The Toxicrene’s mass of tendrils whip and coil about its victim, ensnaring them and drawing them into its lethal embrace.
When the Hive Fleet invades, the skies darken with the descending shapes of hundreds of thousands of Tyrannocytes containing brood upon brood of Tyranids.
Overcome with biochemical adrenaline and predatory aggression, warrior organisms seek constantly to hurl themselves upon the nearest possible prey and tear them to pieces.
This Winged Tyranid Prime was the alpha warrior at the head of the Vardenghast Swarm, which reaped a bloody toll of human prey in a series of battles along the Vardenghast Line.
Scuttling predators that attack in huge swarms, Termagants harry their prey with a hail of firepower, seeking to outflank and envelop their victims as they erode their numbers.
Psychophages stampede into battle with frightening speed, devouring any prey organism in their paths, and using the assimilated energy to bio-stimulate the swarm.
There is no escape from an alpha predator. The Winged Tyranid Prime will use the lesser biocreatures as a distraction to leap onto its prey from above.
What Gordrang lacks in subtlety is more than made up for by the brute savagery and resilience of his horde, who live to rampage and hurl themselves into every fight they can find.
The deafeningly loud noise, scattering of debris over a wide area and atomisation of anyone too close make explosives an irresistible lure to many Orks.
The foul-tempered Boss Nobz are in charge of leading Ork Boyz into battle in huge, unruly mobs that stampede towards the enemy lines.
Some Nobz prefer to fight wielding jaw-droppingly large choppas, ferociously swinging them into battle inflicting mayhem and terror on their foes.
The lunatic Deffkopta pilots hurl ahead of their warband to spy out enemy forces, a process that often finishes with a hazardous blast.
This saw-fisted, bipedal, mechanical abomination is as proficient at terrorizing its foes as it is at dismembering them in a nightmarish scene of carnage.
While Orks delight in the deafening blasts and ferocious recoil of a good firefight, they despise foes that shoot them before they can get stuck into a proper hand-to-hand brawl.
Orks rejoice in aproaching battle in simple and direct ways, and if that approach happens to be while wielding huge, piston-driven, mechanical klaws, even better.
Ork battle strategy rarely stretches far beyond singling out their victims, piling onto them with choppas swinging, and engaging in a spectacle of gratuitous violence.
The more fights an Ork survives, the bigger, meaner, and more covered in scars he becomes. Many Warbosses boast a gnarled green hide as tough as any body armour.
Donning a piston-driven suit of incredibly durable mega armour, Gordrang makes a mockery of his foes' tactics and terrorizes their ranks.
These enormous weapons serve as the mark of a true paragon of brutality amongst orks. Few gits would be able to resist a strike from these massively weighted choppas.
Clad in her highly advanced XV22 Stalker Battlesuit, Commander O’Shaserra employs her strategic genius to orchestrate elaborate plans, destroying the enemy’s most valuable assets.
Aun’Va is the oldest and highest-ranking of the Ethereal Council. His voice is law across the entire T’au Empire. His hand is visible in many of his people’s greatest achievements.
An exemplar among the Fire Warriors of the Vior'la Sept, this hot-blooded commander hurls herself into battle inside her XV86 Coldstar Battlesuit.
Drones feature an armoured shell protecting an AI core, loaded with saviour protocols that compel them to sacrifice themselves for the Greater Good in the place of their masters.
The Fire Caste constitutes the warriors of T’au society. It is their duty to protect the other castes, and to eliminate any foe who opposes the will of the T’au Empire.
MV1 Gun Drones are equipped with pulse carbines that allow them to lay down withering hails of fire.
MV7 Marker Drones are able to ‘paint’ enemy targets for other T’au units to fire upon, while benefiting from increased, networked processing power when present in large numbers.
Missile Drones are a variant of the standard Gun Drone that forgoes the latter’s twin-linked Pulse Carbines armament in favour of a heavier weapon – the Missile Pod.
Pathfinders wreak havoc sniping with potent rifles. Yet their deadliest ability is painting priority targets with massed markerlights for heavier T’au units to annihilate.
The MV5 Stealth Drone is a model that incorporates stealth field generators that can conceal their allies rendering them virtually invisible in open terrain.
Enduring as the most iconic battlesuit, the XV8 Crisis Battlesuit boasts multiple hard points for weaponry and support systems, along with a powerful jet pack.
As much a maverick as he is a master of covert operations, Sub-commander El’Myamoto is a formidable leader of stealth and sabotage missions.
This small but deadly device is deployed by Strike Teams to secure and protect tactical objectives, shooting salvos of smart missiles that leave no hiding place for their foes.
Breacher Teams' pulse blasters are short ranged but deadly, and when coupled with their tough armour and tactical discipline, they become lethal at close quarters.
MV71 Sniper Drones utilize fire-prioritisation routines transmitted by Firesight Marksmen, rendering them smarter, more cunning and even more deadly to distant foes.
Thrumming into battle on membranous wings, this insectile species unleash radioactive salvoes from their neutron blasters while shrugging off damage thanks to their resilient biology.
It is a great honour to be selected as a bodyguard for one of the Fire Caste’s Commanders. These warriors will protect their charge at their own peril without a second thought.
Pulse firearms employ induction fields to propel particles that break down and create focused plasma blasts that can be projected over extremely long ranges.
T’au Ethereals sit at the crossroads of their society’s castes, guiding Fire, Water, Air, and Earth with boundless wisdom and force of will.
These light combat skimmers strike ahead of the main T’au forces, detaching independent weapon drones to sow mayhem behind enemy lines.
Benefiting from jet-assisted speed Stealth Battlesuits make excellent forward operatives who can deploy homing beacons to guide entire insertion forces into battle from low orbit.
Fire Warrior Strike Teams are the mainstay of many Hunter Cadres, unleashing storms of potent anti-personnel firepower that few foes can long endure.
The T’au Empire is a meritocracy in which excellence is recognised with progress. In the Fire Caste this takes the form of advancement through the ranks.
An armoured transport, the Devilfish is an iconic symbol of T’au military expansion. Tough and surprisingly agile, it bears Fire Warriors safely into battle with impressive speed.
Hidden behind shimmering stealth fields, the Firesight Marksmen play their targeting instruments over the foe and transmit data to the MV71 Sniper Drones in their thrall.
A comparatively lightweight and specialist mark of battlesuit, the XV25 Battlesuit conceals its pilot behind fields of lightspectrum and sensor-baffling stealth technology.
The XV88 battlesuit is an indomitable slab of high-tech armour. Its iconic heavy rail rifle and other long-range weaponry can make short work of even the toughest enemy targets.
Those Commanders who exhibit the most aggressive temperaments often choose to take to the field piloting an XV85 Enforcer Battlesuit, based off the enduringly popular XV8 Crisis.
Specialists in infantry-based battlefield tactics, Cadre Fireblades' veteran wisdom is of great benefit to the warriors alongside whom they fight.
This hover tank relies upon other units to use markerlights to highlight targets for its seeker missiles. Once this is done, however, the Sky Ray’s salvoes are nigh inescapable.
The Hammerhead Gunship epitomises the T’au way of war. Resilient and possessing truly ferocious firepower, it also showcases impressive swiftness and manoeuvrability.
A hero to his people, Aun’Shi's presence inspires the T’au of the Fire Caste as surely as a blazing beacon, leading the way to victory with his honour blade flashing and slicing.
The Razorshark is an air superiority fighter with enough resilience and potent firepower to double as an alarmingly effective ground-attack craft at need.
Favoured by Commanders who seek to be everywhere at once, the XV86 battlesuit is capable of soaring at high speed over the battlefield, or even operating in the cold void of space.
Renowned as a tank ace, Longstrike possesses a sublime talent for armoured warfare. His XV02 Pilot Battlesuit allows him to integrate seamlessly with his chosen gunship.
Powered by a thrumming nova reactor, the Riptide battlesuit can overcharge its formidable systems at need, and eradicate entire formations of enemy warriors or armoured vehicles.
Able to micro-manufacture its own energy-munitions in the heat of battle, the Sun Shark drops thrumming pulse bombs onto the foe and obliterates them with ferocious blasts.
These vast ballistic suits are ponderous by T’au standards. A walking gun-tower equal to the mightiest fortress, it anchors the T’au lines while unleashing apocalyptic firestorms.
Roughly translated as ‘the patient hunter’, Kauyon combat tactics rely upon lures to draw the enemy in, before closing the jaws of the trap upon overcommited foes.
The Earth Caste comprises the artisans and engineers of the T’au. It is they who construct machines and ensure the peak performance of the battlesuits for the battles to come.
As a breath of air slips unseen and unheard through blades of grass in a night-time forest, so do the T’au filter swift and silent across the battlefield.
Ethereals control access to numerous classified new technological developments of the Earth Caste, and look for the optimal time to reveal them.
Unification echoes through the ranks, embodying the belief that the life of any given individual of the T’au Empire is of less importance than the needs of the empire itself.
Rather than charge into hand-to-hand combat, T’au soldiery instead intensify their fire patterns and systematically lay waste to the foe.
Some Fire Caste soldiers deploy as elite Pathfinders who scout the foe and mark targets for long-ranged elimination.
As stone resists the onslaught of the other elements in their endless quest to wear it away, so do the T’au exhibit that same unbending resilience.
Engaging all systems, skilled battlesuit pilots can surge into battle in a blaze of deadly-accurate firepower.
The Ethereals perform a unifying role. They take counsel from senior members of each caste, but ultimately all decisions are theirs to make and responsibilities theirs to be borne.
The mere presence of an Ethereal reminds the warriors of the Fire Caste of their place within the Greater Good, and inspires them to even greater efforts.
Pathfinders can infiltrate deep behind enemy lines, to scout the foe and identify the highest priority targets for long-ranged elimination.
Built-in saviour protocols compel the machine intelligence of T'au drones to sacrifice itself for the Greater Good in the place of its masters.
The steady gaze of the Ethereal reminds those of the Fire Caste that there lies within the heart of every storm a zone of silence that remains serene even as fury rages around it.
T’au combined arms groups are called Hunter Cadres for good reason. Working in close coordination, they hunt and destroy the most dangerous enemy targets.
To make best use of their available arsenal, the Fire Caste place heavy emphasis on skilled marksmanship and fighting from a position of advantage.
Swift and lethal, Razorsharks soar over enemy lines raining destruction upon enemy formations as a testament to T'au air superiority and precision tactics.
With mechanical efficiency instilled by endless drills, the T’au maintain a punishing fire rate even when engaging the enemy at long range.
Drones will dive into the path of incoming fire without a second thought if it means protecting T’au lives.
The Greater Good demands the tireless expansion of the T’au Empire. Through diplomacy or strength of arms, new worlds and civilisations are brought into the light of the T’au’va.
The resulting darkness of a solar eclipse allows the usage of low-flying drop ships to deploy entire squads directly into the enemy lines.
As advanced as T'au wargear is, it can also backfire on them. Under harsh battlefield conditions obfuscation flares can detonate prematurely, dousing the battlefield in electro-static interference.
Not all worlds are made equal. Septs were not easy for the T'au to establish. Some worlds are hot, lashed by ferocious natural phenomena and the fiery anger of their star.
To make best use of their available arsenal, the Fire Caste emphasises skilled marksmanship under pressure and the use of firearms over brute force even at close quarters.
These mobile anti-grav gun turrets mount lethal railguns whose hypersonic rounds can stop even super-heavy war engines dead in their tracks.
Tidewall Droneports house swarms of Tactical Drones and shield them from the enemy fire. At a command from the droneport operators, these drones are unleashed to join the battle.
Securing their colossal suits to the terrain, Stormsurge pilots stabilize their firing platforms, unleashing devastating barrages upon their foes with unparalleled precision.
This device deployed by Stealth Battlesuit operatives emits a precise signal that guides Crisis pilots to swiflty descend from a Manta to strike deep within enemy territory.
Powered by an internal microgenerator, this device projects an energy field of substantial scope and resilience able to turn aside even the heaviest incoming fire.
Worn over the eye, sub-commander El’Myamoto's structural analyser allows him to pinpoint the weak spots of even the most indomitable enemies.
Commander O’Shaserra is a master of Kauyon, laying cunning ambushes for her enemies then striking with merciless fury, spearheading these attacks from the front.
Under Aun’Va’s stony gaze, the Hunter Cadres strive to achieve excellence beyond imagining, fighting tirelessly in defence of the Ethereal Supreme.
The T’au make extensive use of machine intelligences they call drones, which carry specialized systems to cover a broad range of battlefield roles.
The Ethereals perform a unifying role within the T’au Empire. On the battlefield, they evoke the elemental truths to inspire nigh-supernatural feats and tide-turning zealotry.
Possessed of fanatical fervour, Ghallaron the Pious leads his forces into the most ferocious war zones, in a quest to receive the boons of the Chaos pantheon.
Ghallaron's mortal followers are zealous worshippers brimming with hate, who see faith as an easy route to power in an uncaring galaxy.
The tales of Ghallaron's feats travel fast, with each new deed from his forces attracting more legionaries eager to join one so blessed by the Dark Gods.
Ghallaron's forces firmly believe that by allying themselves to one so blessed by the Dark Gods, they too will receive the gifts of the Chaos pantheon.
Melta Weapons emit devastatingly intense but short-ranged blasts of heat which can melt through almost any material, with greater effect the closer to the target.
With a preference for inflicting carnage at long range, Havocs rain down death and destruction upon the battlefield.
Havocs wield fearsome weaponry that can tear apart infantry and light vehicles alike with astonishing ease, crippling their enemies' ability to move freely across the battlefield.
These infernal walkers are fitted with a variety of powerful armaments to blast enemies from afar, and cruel appendages with which to hack and crush at close range.
Veterans of the Long War know precisely where to place their shots to inflict the most pain and misery on their luckless victims.
Invoking corruption and pestilence, worshippers of Grandfather Nurgle can bring wondrous diseases upon their unsuspecting enemies.
Some Chaos worshippers make it their primary mission to smash aside all symbols of the enemy faith, in an effort to erase even the records of its existence.
The demagogue's infernal litany calls upon the Dark Gods to offer his foes all manner of whispered temptations, sapping their will to fight.
Fuelled by twisted faith and undying hatred, Chaos warriors strike out with spiteful fury in an endless pursuit of bloodshed.
War Shapers are exemplary warriors that stride into battle armed with symbolic yet deadly traditional weapons, leading Kroot forces in the field.
Swift and vicious, Kroot Carnivores employ fieldcraft and predatory instinct to outwit their foes. Operating in hunting packs, where one is spotted others certainly skulk around.
Driven into a carnivorous frenzy by the scent of blood, Kroot Hounds pounce upon their victims with frightening speed, ripping and tearing with beak-like maws and vicious talons.
Trail Shaper work with instinctive skill to shape the very battlefield upon which the Kroot will meet their prey and guide the routes along which the hunt will progress.
Krootox make excellent living gun platforms, lumbering into battle with cannons strapped to their backs, their Kroot gunners swaying atop their steeds in primitive harnesses.
Flesh Shapers take the Shaper's art of guiding their kin's genetic makeup to a visceral extreme through the use of gruesome flesh-fetishes and ritualised butchery.
Juvenile Krootox exhibit greater aggression and agility than their elders. Used as ambushers, terror troops and skirmish cavalry, they strike fast from unexpected quarters.
Mounted upon chameleonic Kalamandras, Kroot Lone-spears wield explosive javelins. They excel as long-range scouts, picking off valuable enemy targets
Kroot’s quills are powerful sensory organs which, combined with the Kroot’s extremely strong senses of smell and eyesight, help make them formidable trackers and pack hunters.
When the Shapers command, Kroot and Rampagers burst from cover and charge, ploughing headlong into enemy lines and leaping into the fight while voicing shrill avian cries.
Kroot Hounds naturally predate upon weakened foes, drawn by the scent of spilled blood. They are often released in hunting packs that maul vulnerable or fleeing foes.
Kroot Shapers possess an instinctive understanding of their species' morphing biology, and guide the genetic strands of their warpacks through the ingestion of selected prey.
Palatine Erika is a ferociously zealous and experienced war leader, frequently sent to far-flung crusading missions. She inspires her fellow Sisters to fervent acts of bravery.
Appointed Canoness Superior by the grace of the Emperor himself, Junith Eruita sweeps into battle riding within the Pulpit of Saint Holline’s Basilica wreathed in holy fire.
Aggressive, brash and taciturn, Morvenn Vahl leads the Adepta Sororitas from the front in an ancient Paragon Warsuit, smiting her foes with Fidelis and the Lance of Illumination.
Sisters Novitiate are young recruits trained by the Schola Progenium and assigned to an Order Militant to gain combat experience and prove their mettle in the crucible of war.
Battle Sisters of the Orders Militant are skilled and devout warriors. Wherever they advance, the light of the Emperor spreads like a holy dawn and miracles manifest.
Belief in the God-Emperor is the greatest strength of the Sisters of Battle. The force of their faith is expressed in every vengeful shot and every shouted prayer.
These pious bodyguards are chosen for their martial skill and devotion to the Imperial Creed. Bullets and sorcerous witchfire alike are deflected from their warded tower shields.
Fitted with cybernetic weaponry and subdermal stimulants as punishment for past misdeeds, their mindless bodies are energised and unleashed in a frenzied whirlwind of destruction.
Preachers harness the faith of Imperial warriors in battle. Filled with a fearsome religious fervour, they incite the faithful as they bellow catechisms of faith and hatred.
Sisters Repentia charge across the battlefield filled with the need for atonement for past misdeeds, existing only to slaughter the enemies of the Emperor to redeem themselves.
Dominion Squads strike swift and furious, clearing and capturing strategic locations and blunting counter-attacks with vicious salvoes from their flamers and meltaguns.
Retributors are the finest sharpshooters in their Order. They provide heavy fire support as they unleash a storm of bolts and fire upon the enemy.
Wrought from the bones of an ancient saint or martyr, a Simulacrum is carried into battle by a chosen bearer to reinforce the faith of all those who look upon it.
Amalia Novena stands as the embodiment of the values of the Order of Our Martyred Lady, a vengeful and fiery spirit tempered to deliver the God-Emperor's holy justice.
The Celestians are the finest warriors in their Order. They frequently serve as bodyguards and champions of Canonesses, willingly sacrificing themselves to protect their charge.
Missionaries live existences of constant conflict. Fighting at the forefront of the Adepta Sororitas’ holy wars, they stride into battle without fear as they intone sacred prayers.
Some members of the Orders Militant have waged war on hundreds of battlefields. Using their experience, Sister Superiors lead their squads to battle with fervor and determination.
The Dialogus broadcasts her liturgies to her Sisters through their vox-beads and sensor arrays, using inspirational rhetoric of prayers and hymns to exalt praise to the God-Emperor.
The Seraphim fight in the advanced guard, firing with pinpoint accuracy while moving at great speeds and landing with incredible precision to cut down foes in a heartbeats.
Hospitallers are physical and spiritual healers possessed of medicinal expertise. They intone mantras of vigour to dull pain and salve fevered minds.
Obsessed with spilling the blood of the unclean, Death Cult Assassins leap twirling and spinning into the enemy’s ranks. Their every slice and stab has a ritualistic execution.
Channelling all their hatred and fury towards the enemies of Mankind, these warriors storm through the enemy lines with the fervour and force of holy lightning.
Martial and spiritual commanders, Canonesses are both veteran warriors and shining examples of purity. They possess impeccable leadership skills, tactical genius and immense faith.
Topped with the remains of their Saints, this stave represents their heroism in service to the Emperor. Its presence in battle echoes the Saints' deeds, inspiring fellow Sisters.
Imagifiers bear great stanchions in the image of a martyr inscribed with holy texts, and go wherever the fighting is thickest to recite litanies and inspire their fellow Sisters.
As Reliquant at Arms, Aestred is sworn to protect the Auto-Tapestry of the Emperor’s Judgement, which imbues with divine strength those under its presence.
Subjected to terrible agony, Penitent Engines' pilots blaze a trail of destruction with their flamers before charging headlong into the foe, driven by guilt and pain.
Only those who experience a direct and persistent connection with the Emperor become Zephyrim. They are divine  destroyers that strike down their foes with ruthless precision.
Also known as the Daemonifuge, Stern is capable of manifesting strange powers seen by some as witchery, yet she is a zealous defender of the Imperial Creed with firm devotion.
Celestian Sacresants are close-combat specialists who are charged with a holy quest, such as securing sacred relics or purging sites of the unclean.
With shouted prayers and great swings of their maces, Sisters Dogmata demonstrate the path of righteousness and show what the Sisters should expect if they fail in their duties.
Mortifier pilots are Sisters who fled from battle. They cannot move, speak or hear, and suffer endless shame and agony driving them to carve a path of mutilation and destruction.
Saint Celestine is a living embodiment of the Emperor’s might, radiating holy light. Beneath her the faithful are filled with courage, while heretics experience naught but terror.
Those who prove their worth rise to the rank of Celestians, and may be entrusted with a portion of the hallowed truth learnt by their Matriarch in the chamber of the Golden Throne.
This Rhino variant has an aggresive machine spirit, and is equipped with Twin-linked Heavy Flamers primed to cleanse the tainted and sinful from the Emperor's domain.
Every flurry of notes performed by the Exorcist’s artillerist inloads impact coordinates so that volleys of thrice-blessed rockets are fired into the enemy with precision.
At the centre of the Triumph is the blessed bier upon which lie the mortal remains of Saint Katherine. Wherever the Triumph goes, the Emperor’s radiance goes with it.
Paragon Warsuits are regarded as sacred vestments with a noble will of their own. Pilots must have immense faith for the Warsuit’s spirit to trust them.
On the battlefield, sisters are often found delivering His justice with a prayer on their lips and righteous hatred in their eyes. Faith and fury are one and the same in battle.
Deliverers of the Emperor's holy justice, the Adepta Sororitas are unrelenting when facing His enemies, raining down destruction to the clarion call of impassioned prayer.
The miracles of the God-Emperor are self-evident to those with the iron-hard conviction of true zealots. In the presence of the sisterhood, His manifestations are myriad.
The ministrations of the Sisters of the Orders Hospitaller have seen many a warrior brought back from the brink of death to return to the fray.
With purifying flame did the great saints of legend purge the enemies of faith from the galaxy, and such tradition, shall be upheld as long as the sisterhood fights.
With the Emperor watching over them, the righteous zeal of the Sisters of Battle burns ever brighter, fuelling them into miraculous feats in battle.
The faithful stand firm against the worst horrors of the galaxy. Even as hordes of mutants and heretics charge forward, they shall lay them low with righteous fury.
Sisters of Battle gripped with holy fervour banish worldly fears from their minds, shrug off mortal wounds, and summon preternatural strength to smite their foes.
Believed chosen by the God-Emperor Himself, the warriors of the Adepta Sororitas enact miraculous feats on the battlefield, pushing through mortal limitations to enact His will.
The Adepta Sororitas are upheld as the most pious of the Imperial Creed’s adherents, fighting in its name to eradicate any who threaten the purity of Mankind.
Often controlled by the Ecclesiarchy, these planets are the training grounds for members of the Adeptus Ministorum and the Adepta Sororitas.
Saint Katherine was well-known for her fiery determination and vengeful spirit. As long as her relics wage war against mutant and heretic, so shall her deeds continue.
None can escape the Emperor’s judgement. There is no shelter that could withstand the righteous fury of His warriors, nor force that could stop their holy procession.
Girded by their unshakable faith, Sororitas push through the most gruelling hardships to bring death to the Emperor’s enemies. No amount of suffering is too great for them to bear.
A Sister will typically make a pilgrimage to have her wargear bestowed upon her. From that day forth, Sororitas and weapon operate as one to vanquish the enemies of the faith.
Invoking the strength of the God-Emperor through hymns and prayers in the midst of battle, Sisters carve apart their enemies like the warrior-saints of legend.
It is believed that suffering is the greatest prayer a Living Saint can offer the God-Emperor, and a reminder of one's wrongs so that they might strive to correct.
On the battlefield, battle-sisters loudly proclaim their faith in hymn and verse as they march to war, calling upon the Emperor to aid them in the fight against their enemies.
The blood of martyrs is the life force of the Imperium. So do the Sororitas tenets joyously proclaim, and so does the sacrifice of a Sister shine brightest in the darkest hour.
Training and worship are inseparable disciplines to a Sister of Battle. Whilst combat drills and martial studies can hone the body and mind, only prayer can bolster the spirit.
Faith is as strong as any sword. As the sanctified words of the Order’s holy tenets are roared across the halls of the shrine, the devout are infused with the Emperor’s blessings.
When the Ecclesiarchy’s sacred holdings are under threat, the Adepta Sororitas are unleashed in a storm of righteous fire. They stand as their guardians and most zealous defenders.
In the Ecclesiarchy's shrines, statues are raised to exalt the Saints' legendary deeds. Many pray for their guidance, and Sisters invoke their names on the field of battle.
While the shrines of the Adeptus Ministorum are built sturdily, the raging storms on the Shrine Worlds can shake their walls as well as the resolve of those within them.
As well protected as the Shrines can be, a heavy bombardment can still undermine the Shrine defenses and provide unique openings for a swift attack.
Besides waging Wars of Faith, the Daughters of the Emperor devote themselves to a wide range of non-militant disciplines by which they can serve the God-Emperor.
In countless Wars of Faith, Luminas has turned apparent defeat into crushing victory, courageously storming enemy firepoints and assaulting the foe’s elite warriors.
Tales of holy rage, accounts of a martyr's stoicism, stories of miraculous defiance... All serve to inspire and steel the hearts of those adherent to the Imperial Creed.
Holding high the Mace of Castigation, Judith's presence and voice inspire all around her, as she directs the Battle Sisters through the battlefield to where they are most needed.
"With the holy bolter we shall cleanse the mutant, the alien and the heretic. With the Emperor’s gift do we deliver our hatred of the defiler."
Gleaming at her grip, Aveline's Thorn of the White Rose is a symbol of sacrifice, every swing a flaming reminder for her sisters to hold the line no matter the darkness they face.
Once an ambitious and glory-seeking warrior, Aveline's path of trials and sacrifice have made her a deadly, persevering hero capable of bringing down even the most towering foes.
Created to aid the Emperor's servants, these flying cybernetic bio-constructs assist scribe and soldier alike, relaying targeting data and carrying spare ammunition to the frontline.
When the Sisters of the Sacred Rose march to war, they do so in a state of holy grace, their hymns of salvation underscored by the crack of bolts and the roar of burning promethium.
Faith and zealotry are weapons as potent as any blade or firearm. Ministorum Priests embody this truth, bellowing martial canticles to inspire allies and terrify foes.
Rhinos are the mainstay transport of the Adepta Sororitas. Blessed by Enginseers and Ministorum Priests before battle, they are durable, robust, and rarely break down.
Leading squads of Zephyrim, Zephyrim Superiors are divine destroyers, figures of fathomless passion and integrity whose angelic singing drowns out the screams of the dying.
Soaring across the skies like a heavenly messenger, Adelaide sets alight the flame of conviction of her sisters at the break of their resolve, bursting into battle in sparking wrath.
Castigators provide excellent fire support thanks to their wide array of weapons, smashing through enemy lines and slaughtering great swathes of enemy infantry in a matter of seconds.
Even when one of their number falls, the Adepta Sororitas know that this too is part of the Emperor’s plan. A single martyr can spark a fire in a thousand souls.
The Adepta Sororitas go to battle clad in impenetrable conviction and armed with righteous fury. Suffering is their prayer; Faith is their armor.
None may escape the Emperor’s gaze, and where he sees wickedness, there will the Sacred Rose punish.
Chaplain Letharius takes to the field on a Raider-pattern bike, urging his brothers to victory as he bellows his catechisms and charges headlong into the foe.
Fast-moving recon and disruption units, Scout Bike Squads operate far beyond friendly lines. They lay traps on neutral ground and seek out weaknesses in enemy defences.
Outrider Squads conduct lightning-fast hit-and-run attacks on defended positions, and run down those who would try to escape the vengeance of the Chapter.
Techmarines soothe the machine spirits of wounded war engines using their servo-arms and mechadendrites to warp damaged armour plates back into shape and repair burnt-out cabling.
Land Speeders excel at scouting and counter-reconnaissance operations, using the high maneuverability offered by their grav-drives to spot the enemy and call in devastating strikes.
Piloted by veteran warriors and outfitted with silent reactors and servos, Invictor Warsuits excel at supporting vanguard operations and protecting their battle-brothers.
Heavily armed with a gatling cannon and a twin heavy stubber, the Hailstrike can annihilate entire swathes of infantry in fusillades of blistering projectiles.
Predator Annihilators excel at leading armoured spearheads, moving at high speed and firing all the while, blowing apart enemy armoured columns and dense bunker complexes.
In battle, Space Marines swear mighty oaths to destroy the enemies of the Emperor and uphold the honour of their Chapter, and such vows are sacrosanct.
The Space Marines are a highly flexible fighting force, able to swiftly augment their deadly infantry with rugged armoured transports whenever duty calls.
Ultramarines often rely on massed armoured formations during large offensives. Heavy tanks provide fire support while armoured transports relocate infantry across the battlefield.
The Chaplain bellows his fury at the enemy, urging his brothers to surge forward and strike the enemy down with a relentless storm of precise firepower.
A once powerful Overlord, Ramatekh woke from the great sleep with his psyche rent, his ruthless nature wholly focused on driving all living creatures into oblivion.
Even lesser Necron constructs benefit from the technology known as living metal – a semi-sentient substance that can alter its molecular state to heal damage as fast as it is inflicted.
Dynastic legions avoid these cursed beings, whose madness they fear catching, yet they can do little to stop Flayed Ones from being drawn to the scent of bloodshed.
Lokhust Destroyers rely on mobility and firepower to annihilate any life they encounter. Their repulsor-sled bodies allow them to fire on the move without reduction in efficiency.
These hunchbacked monsters burst from their dimensional oubliettes to unleash inescapable hails of enmitic fire leaving no escape to their prey.
Most Necron legions are built around a core of phalanx upon phalanx of infantry. Neurally stunted and grindingly obedient, they are spent freely by their uncaring masters.
Lokhust Lords skim into battle driven by nihilistic hatred. Should they be wounded, nanoscarab amulets spill out a silver tide of mites to repair their rent forms.
Slow-moving but deadly, Annihilation Barges serve as anti-infantry fire support platforms, and are often deployed to watch over important strategic locations.
As the tomb’s warriors pass through a dimensional corridor, the passage’s surface is lit with data-glyphs providing hyperlogical tactical information for the upcoming battle.
The Necrons have slept for sixty million years, if the Aeldari Book of Mournful Night is to be believed. Now they are waking at last, rising up to take back what once was theirs.
Necron nobles make no secret of the fact that they consider the vehicles of their capacious armouries to be more precious than the Necrons who pilot them.
Destroyers can have their corrupted engrammatic patterns reinjected into themselves to further degrade their former personalities and fuel their nihilistic butchery.
The ultimate military leader of the Grizzlepit Convicts, Saffa Rhiannor has spent years preparing for the day she leads the cult into the open and takes over Damnathor V.
As Magus of the Grizzlepit Convicts, Uthrel Naas represents a living promise of salvation to the forlorn convicts that cram the mining pits of Damnathor V.
The strongest and most intelligent of the Grizzlepit’s Acolyte Hybrids, Vorenth earned the honour to bear the sacred wyrm-form banner into battle on the day of the cult's ascension.
Should a Patriarch or Magus dominate a region completely, the psychic shadow around them will grow darker and thicker until it hardens into a many-limbed form known as a familiar.
Neophytes are the dedicated and fanatically loyal foot soldiers of their cult, born of the brood cycle’s third and fourth generations.
Some cultists risk their lives to deploy explosives in key spots of enemy infrastructure. Triggered remotely or by enemy activity, they bring death and freedom in equal parts.
Neophyte hybrids are the least alien in appearance of their brood. What they lack in weaponised bio-adaptations they make up for in numbers, firepower and revolutionary fanaticism.
When the cult signals their attack, Neophytes swarm from sewers, catacombs and shadowy barracks, overwhelming their enemies and seizing control of entire planets within hours.
These merciless xenotainted specialists trigger concealed explosives or lead death-or-glory strikes into the heart of the foe.
Acolyte Hybrids crawl up to the surface firing off volleys of pistol fire, before descending on the enemy in a riot of claws.
The twisted experiments of Grizzlepit Biophaguses led to noticeable improvements in mining output, leading the authorities of Damnathor V to unwittingly provide increasing numbers of test subjects.
An unassuming bodyguard, the Locus may be overlooked by the foe until the exact moment it abandons calm stillness for lightning-fast attack.
The bulkier third-generation brothers and sisters heft the heaviest weaponry, often comprised of stolen military or mining equipment.
Each cult has its own variant of the coiling glyph known as the wyrm-form. The icon’s effect upon its faithful is electrifying, calling them into battle from the shadows they dwell.
On the bloody day of uprising, the Neophyte Hybrids prove themselves as they establish their combat roles, the most capable amongst them naturally assuming command.
Acolyte squads are often lead by the most cunning of their kin, who loyally enact the imperatives of their Patriarch and ignite unity and zeal among the their broodbrothers.
Acolytes are imbued with an echo of their Human parents’ consciousness, granting them an instinctive comprehension of Imperial technologies that aids them in their operations.
Possessed of hulking strength and the skill to manipulate complex mechanisms, Acolyte Hybrids often bear repurposed industrial tools as deadly close-quarters weapons in battle.
Triggered by the approach of a hive fleet or a sudden trauma to the cult, Hybrid Metamorphs mutate, bestowing weaponised limbs and turning into devastating shock troops for the cult.
Nexos can absorb cultists’ thoughts and experiences through physical contact, building a formidable mental map and using it to direct cult forces with prodigious skill.
Vanguard organisms for the Tyranid hive fleets, Purestrain Genestealers combine the cunning of an apex predator with inhuman speed and agility, tearing their victims to bloody tatters.
These lumpen gene-deviants possess immense strength and resilience coupled with simplistic loyalty to the cult, often hurled into battle as line breakers or hulking bodyguards.
Vox-hacker and information assassin supreme, the Clamavus scythes into enemy communications networks and plunders them for intelligence.
This one-man all-terrain bipedal vehicle issued by the Astra Militarum is able to patrol rough terrain, and is often overtaken by cultist insurgents raising in storming rebellion.
In a storm of iron-hard claws, sinewy tentacles and slashing talons, these Metamorphs serve as an inspiration to the broodkin that worship them as sainted heroes of the cult.
A Sanctus is an inescapable assassin who can squirm through the smallest gaps. Once in position, it is only a matter of time before death is delivered to its prey.
Besides the heavy power weapons wielded by most Aberrants, Hypermorphs are also blessed with a chithinous tail that whips and pierces the foe with striking speed.
These light but rugged scout vehicles serve as the eyes and ears of the uprising, coordinating lethal ambushes that eliminate isolated foes or sever communication and supply lines.
These lumbering beasts are dispatched ahead to make a bloody example of those who prove to be an obstacle to the cult.
The occurrence of Hybrid Metamorphs is seen by many broodkin as a great blessing. Many believe that by joining them they will gain favour with the Star Children.
Flitting through the shadows, Reductus Saboteurs lace the battlefield with booby traps and deploy powerful explosives that lay low the engines of war from the oppresors.
Born from the sting of a mindwyrm familiar, the Abominant is an Aberrant tainted with the Patriarch’s own gene-mass, transforming it into a mountain of mutated chitin and muscle.
Robust and versatile, the Goliath Truck is the armoured transport of choice for the Genestealer Cults, able to lay down a hail of supporting fire as the troops disembark into battle.
Whip-fast reactions and hypersensory acuity lend the Kelermorph lethal reaction speeds and help it unleash withering volleys from its iconic liberator autostubs.
A Benefictus uses the swollen mass of their brain to focus the will of the Broodmind, which they unleash in a lancing beam of incredible power.
This mining engine is designed for gouging tunnels into solid rock faces in search of minerals. However, it works just as well as an ablative shield or a bloody linebreaking weapon.
Psychic abomination; alpha predator; parasitic demigod – the Patriarch is all of these things and worse, and the source of the bio-corruption that spawns each Genestealer Cult cell.
Being the core battle tank of the Astra Militarum, Leman Russ Battle Tanks are often a primary target of sabotage missions and grand larceny operations alike.
Genestealer Cults keep their fighting strength carefully hidden from their oppressors. When the day of ascension comes, the long-hidden Cult reveals its subterfuge and rises to attack.
The cultists infesting the myriad Imperial worlds know well that secrecy can be made into a decisive weapon of war.
Cult forces circumnavigate the enemy via crawl-ways or abandoned service tunnels, before bursting forth in sudden ambush.
When the cult throws off its cloak, those infiltrated in the defender's ranks waste no time in spilling the blood of their once comrades, now unfaithful opressors to be removed.
The first hints of Genestealer Cult infestation may come from inexplicable disappearances, thefts of equipment, or the appearance of sinister graffiti praising the Star Children.
In their hidden lairs, Biophaguses trial new bio-alchemical solutions in an attempt to bring out the latent alien power within the brood.
The most xeno-mutant members of the cult take a grim satisfaction in their ability to shrug off horrific damage, as a way to prove their worth and zeal to the Star Children.
Wielding hefty industrial saws and drills, sufficiently determined broodkin can carve their way through the toughest enemy defence lines.
Through genetic alchemy, skilled Biophaguses can tease out favourable mutations without triggering any undesirable degradations, rendering their subjects increasingly deadly.
On the day of ascencion, each Magus becomes a focal point for cult forces, a potent battle psyker who can drive their brothers and sisters into frenzied violence.
No matter how large a Genestealer Cult grows, it is typically dominated by a single Patriarch via the synaptic link known as the Broodmind.
The convicts of Damnathor V proved to be an excellent vector for the Curse. Their desire for liberation after decades of forced labour has paved the way for the cult to spread.
During a cult’s gestation, the Magus wages a war of honeyed words and psychic domination. An audience with a Magus can turn almost any human into a valuable agent of the cult.
Those who are blessed with the blood of the Starborn will stand victorious beneath the sigils of the cult once the last shot is fired and the last body falls.
Multitudes emerge in secret from dorms and the crannies of the merciless pits. Minutes before the revolt, the cult gathers for a final prayer, for the Day of Ascension has come.
Thanks to a mixture of cunning, instinct and guerrilla fieldcraft, the brood bursts from cover without the slightest warning, giving no time for their foes to register their peril.
From duct-tangles and sewage pipes to subterranean mineworks and sappers’ runs, the Genestealer Cults employ all imaginable types of hidden ways to better ambush their foes.
Even as battle rages, reinforcements slip from the shadows or spill up from the dark places below, called to war by the Broodmind.
Through extending the tendrils of the Broodmind into the psyche of the enemy, Genestealer Cults win allies to their cause, infecting them with the genecurse of the cult.
The cults project a psychic signal that not even the faithful are aware of. As their synaptic Broodmind grows, it becomes a glimmering beacon that the Tyranid hive ships home in on.
On the Day of Ascension the broodkin strike at multiple targets with uncanny cohesion. Detonations rock the population centres and transport arteries, hindering the shocked defenders.
The mayhem of belligerence can cause mine tunnels to collapse, closing some pathways whilst opening new ones, which only the most attentive commanders can use to their advantage.
The wreckage of battle can cause sump containments to collapse and flood subterranean halls, hampering the deployment and positioning of troops fighting underground.
The ducts and pipelines of the mines in Damnathor V are filled with toxic chemicals. Hazardous leaks are one of the many travails of mining crews in this penal colony.
Echoing through dank caverns, the cult followers worship the Patriarch and the Star Children, gathering around alien idols of iron, flesh and bone.
Wild-eyed hordes of cult warriors dwell in the sewers, mine workings and rusted ducts, waylaying their oblivious victims.
Breaking the enemy supply chains will bring the unbelievers down to their knees. Break their engines of war, sever their bridges and topple their fanes.
The Primus is a Genestealer Cult’s ultimate military commander. Their mastery of insurgent tactics transforms their followers from a rebellious mob into a lethal military machine.
The prophetic leader guides the cult to new heights of victory as the Patriarch’s mind-altering influence spreads further over the host populace.
It is a great honour to bear the cult’s sigil aloft for all to see. Its presence upon nearby cult warriors is electrifying, driving them to new heights of violence.
When the day of ascension comes, Patriarchs become the cult’s deadliest killer, prowling the shadows of embattled worlds to rip and slay.
Skilled cult agents spread disinformation and demoralising propaganda, invading the very minds of enemy personnel, rendering them puppets to the cult and recruiting new followers.
Military communications are essential to combat operations' efficiency. One broken link opens the gates for miscommunication, chaos and tactical blunders.
Devious contaminants infect their victims with xenos genetics, rendering them ill and susceptible to the sinister influence of the cult.
Fashioned from munition crates and fuel barrels, makeshift blockades are often assembled at seemingly random spots, later proving highly disruptive to enemy reinforcement manoeuvres.
The innovative methods of the Biophaguses extend the reach of the cult far and wide. They infect their subjects with xenos genetics, morphing their body and mind.
Clamavuses are masterful agents of misinformation who use their vox-interceptor arrays to hack into enemy communications networks, stealing vital intelligence.
Lhaska Szenari is a revered Jackal Alphus with the endurance to travel on her dirtcycle for days, gathering vital information and setting up deadly, war-changing shots.
These fourth-generation hybrids roar through tunnels and dusty plains to gather intelligence on trade routes, military outposts, resource deposits and the like.
Atalan Jackals harass the foe with hit-and-run strikes. They share a mental link that allows them to coordinate in hunting packs and ride in tight formations at high speeds.
Serving their gene-sect as outriders, these packs act as a swift reconnaissance and raiding force, picking off weak or isolated enemy units and harassing the foe’s flanks.
Atalan-class vehicles are standard issue work transports on almost every Imperial world. Riding these, the Jackals pose as operatives for mining corporations or aqua prospectors.
Atalan Leaders roam under the blazing suns of the frontier worlds along with their mechanised gangs and fall upon the cult’s enemies like meatstarved scavengers.
Wolfquads provide heavy support to Atalan Jackals squads, using light prospecting vehicles whose mining lasers and gear are turned from tools of progress into weapons of war.
A utilitarian vehicle intended for geological surveying and running messages between isolated communities, the Ridgerunner excels in scouting missions for the cult.
As the cult grows, its scions infiltrate the fortified compounds of the Enforcers and Adeptus Arbites to ensure the local authorities continue to overlook the cult’s operations.
Through constant harassment tactics, Atalan Jackals can misdirect their enemies’ attention and leave them wide open to attack from an unexpected quarter.
Cutting supply lines and reinforcement routes is vital to ensure the insurgence's success. Valuable assets are targeted where possible, sometimes with a spectacular result.
The Jackal Alphus rides its dirtcycle to vantage points calling in strike missions with its long-range vox and dispatching any foe beneath the cross hairs of their cult sniper rifle.
Former Captain of the Ultramarines, Titus was suspected of heresy due to his natural resistance to the Warp. Ultimately exonerated, he now serves the chapter as a Lieutenant.
To Titus, combat is as natural as breathing. After countless battles against the foes of humanity, he is as adaptable as he is deadly.
Often fighting against impossible odds, Titus' fury burns hot as he refuses to fall, even when all seems lost.
The tribulations faced in multiple campaigns have now made of Titus what many Astartes consider an inspiring paragon of the virtues of the Ultramarines.
Trained with many weapons, Titus often wields a Thunder Hammer, discharging vast amounts of disruptive energy and a deafening thunder-like sound upon each impact.
Arcadian Leontus is responsible for all Astra Militarum within the Segmentum Solar. He hails from a peerless lineage of service dating back countless generations.
Ursula Creed is her father’s daughter in many respects. A hardened general, physically imposing, Creed stands as a symbol of Cadia’s survival, exemplifying her people’s unbowed spirit.
As feared as he is respected, Commissar Elan Denkler keeps his troops in line with ruthless efficiency, having molded them into a disciplined war machine few other officers can match.
Since the Great Rift's opening, the Aurora Illuminato fills Faeburn's skies, which is seen by the Vanquishers as a sign from the Emperor, bringing both nightmares and solace.
The tough combat medics of the Astra Militarum have dragged screaming soldiers back into service time and again, telling them that the Emperor is not ready for them that day.
Diminutive, keen-eyed and instinctively stealthy, the abhuman Ratlings serve the Astra Militarum primarily as outstanding snipers.
The Shock Troops of Cadia have trained their entire lives for military service, and they are held by many as the first and main line of defense of the Astra Militarum.
Squads are often provided with specialist equipment and additional training, including expert vox operators who relay the Company Commander’s orders to the men on the front lines.
These gun crews can swiftly set up their mobile heavy weapons to bolster battle lines, providing close fire support with adaptable load-outs of precise or indiscriminate firepower.
Heavy infantry regiments are often granted exotic armaments such as flamers or plasma guns, ensuring the regiment’s infantry are always supported by tremendous firepower.
Disciplined and professional, the Kasrkin are peerless soldiers, the elite of the elite. These special operatives launch precision strikes against the enemies of the Imperium.
These attaché artillery officers feed targeting information to distant ordnance crews, calling upon them to deliver deadly munitions where they are most needed.
While lacking great intelligence, these abhumans are patiently trained to understand orders. Once their strength and resilience is tamed and directed, they are nigh on unstoppable.
The Astra Militarum, for all its extension and decentralised organisation, is built on a rigid hierarchy. A fortified chain of command exists, ensuring every soldier knows their place.
Minka Lesk was there when Cadia fell – she remains as Cadia Stands, a testament to the indomitable Cadian will. Now a respected captain, she fights on to honour the brave souls lost.
Psykers in service of the Scholastica Psykana, Astropaths aid the soldiers of the Imperium with their ability to divine the shifting psychic currents amidst the swirl of combat.
Hailing from the steppes of Attila, these horsemasters are potent cavalry troops. Their mobility makes them a powerful force, whether spearheading an attack or outflanking the foe.
Every regiment has a number of standards that are carried in battle by a Command Squad. Each company will have its own standard, embroidered with the names of their fallen heroes.
Commissars are ruthless officers charged with maintaining the morale, discipline and fighting spirit of their regiment. Their devotion to the Imperium is without doubt.
Scout Sentinels' lighter armour and gyro-stabilisers assist them in swiftly traversing the roughest terrain, enabling their pilots to survey the enemy with ease.
Enginseers use arcane lore and cybernetic arrays to effect repairs upon damaged fighting war engines, priceless artefacts of technology whose spirit need only be roused once more.
