Modified with extra protective panelling, Armoured Sentinels are superb front-line hunters, wielding heavy weapons across terrain too cramped for battle tanks to operate on.
Amongst the largest man-portable weapons, these guns crewed by ordnance teams fire fire heavy shells and warheads, providing heavy-hitting weapons that can reach across the battlefield.
The most obstinate of the Ogryn strain of abhumans, Bullgryns are clad in heavy armour and carry crude assault weaponrys, advancing in shield-lines from which shots bounce harmlessly.
These battle-trained psykers support the Astra Militarum with eerie foretelling, warding soldiers against the enemy’s witchcraft and unleashing tempests of their own psychic might.
The Taurox is a swift armoured transport with armoured tracks that enable it to cross difficult terrain with ease, exploiting gaps in the enemy lines before deploying its passengers.
Cadian Castellans are authoritative leaders who bear a panoply of armaments and insignia, wielding their weapons as skilfully as they command the soldiers beneath them.
A workhorse armoured troop carrier, the Chimera is a durable and practical tank, employed to ferry infantry into the harshest war zones.
The Hydra is an anti-aircraft flak tank equipped with an array of specially adapted autocannons. Once it locks on to enemy aircraft, none can escape its storm of shells.
Nork Deddog’s loyalty and his skills as a bodyguard are beyond question. The hulking Ogryn would rather sustain terrible wounds than permit a single scratch on those he protects.
Firing at incredible distance, its limited supply of storm eagle rockets release multiple warheads a moment before each rocket’s impact, leaving no escape to the panicking foe.
Basilisks are self-propelled artillery tanks, armed with a fearsome earthshaker cannon, capable of unleashing relentless shelling at vast distances.
The Leman Russ is the core battle tank of the Imperial Guard, forming the spearhead of countless armoured attacks, capable of facing down almost any battlefield target.
Well-armed and heavily armoured, Valkyries are agile carrier-gunships with experienced crews that drop payloads of soldiers both at low-level or high altitudes via grav-chutes.
No other battle tank of the Imperial Guard possesses more raw stopping power than the Vanquisher, which offers a long range, first-hit kill ratio second to none in anti-tank weaponry.
Maelon Dhrost is a veteran of over one hundred and fifty gruelling years of war, every one of which has been spent fighting the scourge of Chaos that blights his native soil.
The immense Rogal Dorn Battle Tank is a lumbering behemoth equally suited to anchoring a battle line or grinding forward in support of an assault.
This super-heavy rolling fortress possessed of overwhelming firepower, takes the centre of the battle line to shelter Imperial Guardsmen and even smaller tanks in its lee.
Regiments of numerous origins and tactical roles inculcate their soldiers from an early age with the legendary doctrines of the Tactica Imperium.
When necessity arises, mechanised crews rouse their engines, pushing past tolerances to roll forward at speed and outmanoeuvre the foe.
When need dictates, Imperial Guard soldiers are ordered to move doubletime to close with the enemy or secure an open flank.
Via area denial bombardments or delayed blast shells, tank crews can paralyse enemy advances, pinning down the swiftest foe.
Many light infantry regiments specialise in stealth and scout tactics, reconnaissance missions and unorthodox warfare, using the environment to their best advantage.
All Cadians – no matter their age, gender or station – must know how to fight, and be capable of facing with unwavering courage all the horrors that proliferate in the 41st Millennium.
The brutish ripper guns added to the raw power and muscle of the hulking, abhuman Ogryns lunged upon the enemy result in a shock troop able to deliver devastating charges.
Wise Astra Militarum commanders gather talented second officers, advisers, tacticians and front-line strategists to perfect just as many strategic responses as the situation demands.
With their officer’s clarion call in their ears, soldiers lose all sense of doubt, faith shielding their souls from malevolence and marching at full pace to fire upon their enemy.
Attrition often forces fragmented regiments to merge their formations, learning new skills to fight together and continue to wage the Emperor’s wars.
With the power to summarily execute any soldier or officer found wanting, Commissars are feared, brooding figures that can turn the Guardman's fear into a deadly advantage.
The searing touch of thermal weaponry can flush enemies out of their cover and spread destruction. From handheld to heavy flamers, there is no hiding from the flames.
Though Cadia fell, the mantra 'Cadia stands' lives on. For Cadia does indeed still stand, as long as a single Cadian soldier continues to fight.
In the face of overwhelming odds, pinpoint shelling from attached artillery tanks and rapid advances by armoured squadrons can turn the tide of battle with crushing results.
Where sheer volume of heavy ordnance is concerned, few can compete with the Astra Militarum. Siege formations shell targets into oblivion as foot soldiers advance to secure victory.
The Astra Militarum is the shield of Mankind. Only by its sacrifice and heroism are the worlds of the Imperium kept safe.
Mechanised regiments enable more troops to enter the fight even under heavy enemy fire, conditions in which footslogging Imperial Guardsmen would otherwise soon perish.
Soldiers continuing to uphold the lineage of the bastion world yearn to visit destruction on those responsible for the fall of Cadia.
The sanctioned use of a Deathstrike – designated ‘Ordnance Extremis’ – is often an excessive measure to combat most heinous enemies, a catastrophe delivered from half a world away.
Siege warfare, as practised by the Astra Militarum, is amongst the most dehumanising, miserable and filth-ridden modes of fighting there is.
A war scholar, polyhistor and martial tactician, the Lord Commander Solar’s razor-sharp intellect and energetic leadership belie his extensive command experience of more than a century.
Ursula has restlessly demanded swift redeployment in the wake of victory after victory, forging her own legend as a strategist of incredible intuition and ruthless determination.
Once orders have been given and plans are in motion, Commissar Denkler joins the fight where the battle is thickest, setting an inspirational example for those under his command.
A bodyguard of legendary repute, Nork displays an uncommon level of mental aptitude. In the rare instances when his charge is wounded, allied soldiers may even look to Nork for orders.
Unbroken by the fall of her homeworld, Minka Lesk's indomitable faith and the memory of her fallen comrades drive her forward to fight for Cadia no matter the cost.
Trained for rapid response, Shock Troopers are deployed to the battlefield at crucial moments, bringing discipline and firepower exactly when and where it’s needed.
To many Astra Militarum officers, the best defence is overwhelming firepower. Enemies raiding Imperial outposts often find themselves gunned down before they can even glimpse the walls.
The Departmento Munitorum is responsible for munitions, supplies, recruitment, training and support, both medical and technical.
The first light of dawn offers a moment of opportunity. The rising sun blinds the unprepared, giving cunning commanders the perfect moment to advance their troops into position.
The shock of a planetary invasion can leave defenders scrambling, as indiscriminate orbital fire and the chaos of multiple open fronts lead to extreme consequences on any frontline.
As the demands of war grow, factories roar into overdrive, pushed to their limits to churn out munitions and war machines at an accelerated pace, at the risk of perilous breakdowns.
Clad in an intimidating greatcoat, Tempestor Prime Hektor Thenmann is a veteran of countless missions who marshals his elite soldiers into the perfect position for the task at hand.
Deployed by Tempestus Aquilon Squads, these automaton servo-sentries provide additional firepower as the assault is pressed home.
Fanatically dedicated to the act of following their orders, Tempestus Scions complete missions so dangerous that they would be deemed suicidal for a regular Guardsman.
Guided by a Tempestor Sergeant, a full unit of Scions can change the tide of a war with a single strike, gravchuting from the ramps of Valkyries, or bursting from their Taurox Primes.
Deployed amidst battle, these Scions are issued medi-packs that contain all the necessary drugs, dressings and surgical tools to get a wounded Tempestus Scion back in the fight.
Hand-picked for their violent nature, Tempestus Aquilons deploy by grav-drop, descending from the skies to land precisely where their destructive firepower is most keenly required.
Only the exceptional can stand out among the Tempestus Aquilons. Vitus Gryf has earned such honour, guiding her scions through countless successful counter-xeno operations.
Thick armoured plates, quad track units and a supercharged engine allow the Taurox to go anywhere, hurtling across ruined cities and rubble-strewn wastelands with equal speed.
In the ancient, harsh training camps based on long-established Imperial worlds, the orphaned offspring of the Imperium are transformed into ruthless soldiers and efficient killers.
Valkyries possess the speed and armour to deliver the Tempestus Scions where they are needed. Afterwards, they hover over the battlefield raking enemy troops with heavy weapons fire.
The regiments of the Militarum Tempestus depend upon their Taurox Primes to deliver the fury of the Imperium across all manner of hazardous war zones and almost impossible conditions.
The Tempestor Prime commands the finest human soldiers in the galaxy. Its ranks boast the elite Scions of the Militarum Tempestus, who launch blistering strikes with ruthless efficiency.
Quick to anger and with a especially vehement hatred of Chaos, even for a Space Marine, Chairon is a relentless warrior who has vowed to avenge his fallen brothers.
Clad in thick Gravis armour, Heavy Intercessors are immovable defenders who secure ground and lay down volleys of heavy fire that keep all but the most persistent enemies at bay.
Thanks to their heavier Mk X power armour, Eradicators stride unharmed through waves of incoming fire before bringing their own destructive weaponry to bear at close range.
Members of their Chapter’s elite 1st Company of Veterans, these inexorable warriors advance relentlessly with blades held high – the very image of noble knights of myth.
These peerless assassins are deadly marksmen who haunt the shadows of the battlefield unseen by the enemy. Their sophisticated scopes ensure they never fail to make the kill.

Trained to be a paragon of duty, Gadriel embodies the Ultramarines values of strict adherence to discipline, tactical prowess, and dedication to the Emperor’s service as dictated in the Codex Astartes.
Serving aboard the battle barge Resilient, Valtus was a 2nd company veteran before being fatally wounded and interred as a Redemptor Dreadnought.
The Codex Astartes explains in detail the strategic value of overwhelming firepower applied to key targets at the optimal time in order to eliminate threats and create tactical openings.
As the warring armies close upon one another and vicious firefights erupt, the Codex lays out strategies for swiftly seizing the initiative and combining versatility with firepower.
The Codex Astartes leaves no doubt that the killing blow in most engagements must be delivered with a decisive close-quarters strike. It presents plentiful tactical means to achieve this end.
Azrael is arguably the greatest to ever hold the title of Supreme Grand Master. Deeply committed to his Chapter’s secret agenda, the hunt for the Fallen is never far from his mind
Belial was promoted to Grand Master of the Deathwing after facing none other than Ghazghkull Thraka and, outnumbered thousands to one, stalling the Orks and saving Piscina IV.
Asmodai is the Dark Angels’ Master Interrogator-Chaplain and Master of Repentance. His talents for torture and interrogation first made themselves known during the Macharian Heresy.
Most of the wars the Dark Angels partake in have little or nothing to do with the Fallen, though they scour every battlefield for signs of sedition, corruption and Human augmentation.
These warrior-medics stride through volleys of gunfire and vicious melees to aid their wounded brothers and recover the progenoid glands of those who cannot be saved.
An experienced officer of the 5th Company, Sergeant Taaman is adept at the unexpected yet brutally effective strikes Reivers are known for, sowing fear and confusion amongst the foe.
Regardless of their battlefield tasks, when the Ravenwing fight they strike at precise moments, gunning into action in a burst of thunderous acceleration.
The Dark Angels’ organisation largely follows that of the Codex Astartes, with its third through tenth companies organised alongside Codex lines.
Spearheading devastating offences and shattering enemy assaults, Aggressors are walking ceramite strongpoints who lay down torrents of devastating fire at close-quarters.
The Ravenwing Black Knights are the 2nd Company’s greatest warriors, elite fighters who style themselves after the monster-hunting knights of old Caliban
On every tier of the Chapter’s organisation, the Dark Angels have a vast array of ancient rites and traditions –such as the Feast of Malediction– led by their Chaplains.
Company Veterans are elite warriors and highly experienced fighters. They are their Captain’s bodyguard, closest advisors and the core of his command squad.
Masters of the Interromancy Discipline, Dark Angels Librarians contribute to the Hunt both on the battlefield as well as on interrogations, inscribing heretics on the Book of Salvation.
Though none in the 2nd Company bar the Grand Master and Black Knights are aware, the Ravenwing’s primary role in the Chapter is to hunt down the Fallen amongst the ravaged enemy forces.
The Ravenwing Champion is gifted a deadly Blade of Caliban – an ancient power sword as old as the Chapter itself, and tasked with cutting down the most formidable opponents
Captains have spent centuries with their Chapter. They expect nothing but utter dedication from those they command.
Deploying to the battlefield via teleport strike or armoured transport, Deathwing Terminators unleash devastating firepower before closing in to annihilate their foes in melee combat.
The Inner Circle Companions are some of the most skilled and sinister warriors. They arrive unannounced to guard heroes of the Unforgiven or pursue secret quests.
The Interrogator-Chaplains’ hatred for the Fallen runs deep. Dour individuals, their minds are set to a single purpose: right the terrible wrongs of their Chapter’s past.
As Keeper of the Unseen Ritual, Lazarus is responsible for collating knowledge of Caliban’s ancient orders, much of which is held only by the Inner Circle.
With a larger chassis and superior anti-gravity engines than the standard Land Speeder the Vengeance can mount heavier weaponry while keeping pace with the fastest ground vehicles.
Those machines that have served the Dark Angels the longest, or with greater accomplishments, have their venerable machine spirits fortified by the Techmarines' rites of great honour.
Members of the Dark Angels' elite 1st Company of Veterans, each of these vastly experienced Space Marines has fought to preserve the Imperium across uncounted worlds.
Company Champions meet the foe’s greatest warriors in single combat to defend the honour of their Chapter and to free up their commanders to lead and coordinate the strike force.
Equipped with heirloom wargear, Deathwing Knights teleport into the heart of the thickest fighting, their strikes breaking the enemy’s back in one fell swoop.
The Ravenwing Ancient carries one of the company’s sacred standards, and beneath its shadow the black-armoured warriors of the Ravenwing bring death to the foe.
Mounted in a Land Speeder outfitted with additional auspex scanners and vox-casters, it is a Talonmaster’s role to direct the Ravenwing’s fire.
To this day, only the Deathwing, select Masters, the Interrogator-Chaplains and Librarians of the Chapter have any real knowledge of the Unforgiven’s past and its hidden knowledge.
Upon each Darkshroud there is a mysterious statue that survived Caliban’s destruction and became imbued with energies that can obscure nearby battle-brothers from enemy sight.
Strikemasters serve as the Deathwing’s Lieutenants. They have carried out deeds of enormous bravery on countless battlefields, honing their skills as warriors and leaders.
As Grand Master of the Librarius and Keeper of the Keys, Ezekiel can open all portals on the Rock, save but a handful, and has the ability to read the intentions of any individual.
The most formidable fighter of his company, the Deathwing Champion wields a halberd of Caliban. His wide swings strike down multiple foes as he seeks out the most worthy opponents.
Air-to-air interceptors, Nephilim Jetfighters perform lightning-fast warfare manoeuvres. These pilots continually push the Techmarines for enhancements and modification to their craft.
As time went by, the number of warriors who witnessed what befell on Caliban dwindled to none but a handful of ancients interred within Dreadnought sarcophagi.
The Dark Talon possesses strange armaments dating back to the Dark Age of Technology, and is designed to snatch up the Ravenwing’s prey.
Sammael rides to war on the jetbike Corvex, a relic from the Dark Age of Technology. Upon this ancient mount, the Ravenwing’s commander charges with the Raven Sword.
Led by a Knight Master, the arrival of Deathwing Knights upon a battlefield is portentous, for they are rarely deployed without great need or the prospect of the Fallen’s presence.
Clad in advanced armour plating and armed for any battlefield situation, the Repulsor not only transports its passengers safely, it also provides superb fire support.
Strikemasters have the onerous duty of managing the gaols deep within the Rock, where the most treacherous prisoners are held and the most dangerous relics secured.
After Horus’ rebellion failed, the Imperium was left in a state of turmoil. The Inner Circle was formed during that time, a closed network of the Dark Angels’ most senior warriors.
A number of Deathwing accompany most Dark Angels strike forces, not only for their outstanding martial might, but also so that they can undertake secret missions.
Scout teams are often sent to seek for the Fallen. The hunt has never ceased and never will until all are captured, though the Unforgiven can fight for decades with no sign of them.
The stalwart descendants of the Lion are renowned for their unshakeable resolve, enduring tenacity and strict fire discipline in battle.
Though most Dark Angels have little idea what it is they are searching for, those of the Inner Circle understand the subtle clues that might aid them in hunting the Fallen.
Even for a Chapter as famously stubborn as the Dark Angels, some warriors are known for their intractable nature. Utterly persistent, even death is not enough to stay their wrath.
The Dark Angels have had no home world since Caliban was shattered. The Rock is all that is left of that world, a voidborne hunk of solid rock fitted with enormous engines.
The STC for the Nephilim Jetfighter was discovered on the hunt for the Fallen Baelor the Imposter. The technology – named the Lionheart engine – was used to modify older designs.
Through rigorous training and countless battles endured, the Deathwing have learned to begin their sweeping fire patterns immediately upon their arrival from teleportation.
The Fallen’s existence is a persistent stain on the Dark Angels' honour. For the Unforgiven to be redeemed, their traitorous brethren must be hunted down and made to repent.
Symbolizing the defiance for which the Dark Angels are famed, the Standard of Devastation has flown above numerous last stands, often found atop piles of enemy dead.
The enemies of the Emperor must be dug out of every bolthole and tainted strongpoint, driven from their heretical fastnesses and subjected to the merciless judgement of the Unforgiven.
Cutting down the last of their foes and giving no mind to their own hurts, the Unforgiven press relentlessly on toward victory.
Many foes have charged the Dark Angels’ lines, only to be met by an unbreakable wall of ceramite, while the Dark Angels channel all their focus and aggression to smash the foe.
The Dark Angels march to war with sombre determination. Merciless and relentless, they systematically slaughter their enemies until nothing remains but corpses and blazing wreckage.
The Dark Angels wage entire wars to secure individuals who might have knowledge of the whereabouts of the Fallen, or who may have acquired a fragment of the Dark Angels’ secrets.
Boarding infested space hulks, carrying out unsupported alpha-strikes or attacking the most horrific enemies, the Dark Angels will go to any lengths to carry out their secret missions.
Black-clad huntsmen and masters of the art of lightning warfare, the Ravenwing race before their Chapter like thunder before a storm.
Undeniable is their loyalty. Undeniable is their zeal. Undeniable is their fury. Among the Adeptus Astartes it is them who have stood the longest, bled the most and wavered least.
Azrael is a beacon of inspiration to those who follow him, and is paid enormous respect for his ability as a strategist, orchestrating his forces to maximum advantage.
Belial’s combat technique has no great style, flourish or artifice. Instead it is driven by ruthless killing efficiency and well-honed strength. Each parry and thrust is a decisive act.
Asmodai does not suffer fools of any kind. His interests lie only in the Chapter’s goals and in battle. Such is Asmodai’s motivation, many of his actions border on the indefensible.
Sammael is a master of high-speed warfare, able to react to changing battlefield situations in the blink of an eye and deploy the Ravenwing to wherever they are most needed.
Usually at the forefront of battle, Ezekiel is a master of Interromancy. His warp-whispers claw away the sanity of his enemies, while his blade rends their flesh.
Enemy commanders are oblivious of the explosive value of the knowledge they hold. The Librarians of the Dark Angels are adept at scanning the minds of their foes for any clues.
The Unforgiven act without hesitation or mercy should they receive the merest hint that their foes have gleaned knowledge of their hidden secrets.
The Dark Angels swiftly agreed that what transpired on Caliban was to be kept secret at all costs, and were sworn to silence to prevent being declared Excommunicate Traitoris.
The Unforgiven honour successful warriors through ancient and obscure rituals, rewarding them –if deemed ready– with advancement into the inner mysteries of the Chapter
Even after winning glorious victories, Chaplains give each combatant their own specific penance, whether it be battle drills, hymnals or rites of atonement.
What may look as mere rites and ceremonies often conceal the truth of the Chapter through circles of metaphor and allegory, where crucial information of The Hunt is secretly conveyed.
Larger than the heaviest class of Imperial warship, The Rock is fitted with a vast range of formidable defensive weapons, cavernous docking bays and wide-reaching comms arrays.
Used by the Imperium to power voidships, hive cities and more, Plasma Generators are advanced reactors that generate power through nuclear fusion, harnessing high-temperature plasma.
Unlike most Chapters, the Unforgiven do not possess a home world. Instead, The Rock navigates the galaxy as The Hunt demands, often exposing itself to the calamities of outer space.
While heavily protected, the lack of a large gravitational field and an atmosphere normally found in planetary fortresses allows for voidcrafts to be used in an assault against orbital stations.
The magnetic fields of stars can help conceal orbital stations from enemy sensors; however, once located, stellar flares can also make them vulnerable to a well-timed attack.
There’s not a tougher or more belligerent Ork than Mozrog Skragbad. Boasting a craggier hide than a rok squig’s, he is the epitome of what the average Beast Snagga aspires to become.
Mozrog and his squigosaur steed Big Chompa can weather the worst any foe throws at them. The few enemies that survive Big Chompa's jaws are teared by Mozrog's his kustom punch‑dagger.
Ferocious and foul‑tempered, beastboss Morgrim possesses cybork enhancements and a wired‑in targetin’ squig to bring down even the largest prey one‑on‑one.
Beastbosses must constantly prove themselves the biggest and baddest fighters, seeking out and pulverising the foe’s most dangerous champions in gory displays of superiority.
There isn’t a problem that Beast Snaggas don’t think can be fixed with a squig. As for the nimble grots that fight alongside them, they adhere to such statement the best they can.
Big, brutal, and belligerent Beast Snaggas excel in softening up their prey, dragging them down, then ripping them bodily to bits.
Thanks to the spirited – if inexpert – surgery by painbosses' grot orderlies, lucky fell orks may eventually get back on their feet for more krumpin'
Often announcing an imminent stampede of Beast Snaggas, the fist-shells of their thump guns pour upon enemy lines, with their fierce blast making up for the shooter's lack of accuracy.
Beast Snagga Nobz easily lead their packs of boyz into the fight, a task merely consisting on bellowing louder than the foe and rushing faster than fellow Orks to get krumpin' first.
Accostumed to the ways of their tribe, even the nimblest of Grots will try their luck at riding squigs into battle, many a Grot meeting their end chomped by the very squig they ride.
Runtherds possess a deep understanding of how to rear, train and herd the squigs and runts that keep Ork society functioning, not knowing nor caring where their knowledge comes from.
The average Ork has as much time for military organisation as they do for washing regularly. Combat structures are as rough‑and‑ready as they are instinctive.
Should a Rig be wrecked, the draught Tramplasquig will find itself set loose amidst the bellowing of war, and will run amok stomping any fool in the way of the untethered beast.
This wild‑eyed wanderer knows the secrets of breeding the best and baddest runts, and sells his peculiar services to the highest bidder.
Leading the packs of Squighob boys into the fray, these Nobz ride thick‑skulled smasha squigs, employing their muscle, weight and momentum to squash their foes to a paste.
With their mounts snorting and saddlegitz hanging on for dear life, Squighog Boyz thunder into the fight, flinging rokkit‑propelled stikkas with enough force to pierce plate armour.
Highly respected in Beast Snagga society, Wurrboys employ their pseudo‑shamanic powers to glean visions they believe are sent by Gork and Mork, guiding them to the best prey.
When a Beastboss wishes to ride a Squigosaur, he must first beat it within an inch of its life to teach it respect, all without getting devoured in the process.
Weirdboyz have little or no control over their dubious yet powerful gifts. When Waaagh! energy starts flowing, a great portion of that energy flows straight into nearby Weirdboyz.
Welded, lashed and nailed together from enemy wrecks and scavenged scrap, the Hunta Rig's open metal deck ushers chanting mobs of Beast Snagga Boyz to ride along on the hunt.
Whilst, fulfilling both roles of Meks and Painboyz, Painbosses prefer to work on squigs than on Orks and, frankly, most of their Beast Snagga patients would prefer it that way too.
The Kill Rig’s stikka kannon fires rokkit‑harpoons big enough to wrangle battle tanks, yet it is the Wurrboy atop his wurrtower that both enemies and Beast Snaggas fear the most.
Often reinforced with the salvaged parts of their latest prey, Snakebite's Battlewagons' are one of the few 'propa' know-wotz they tolerate; as long as it gets te boyz krumpin' faster
Squiggoths can grow in size indefinitely. The larger they get, the more prized. Kitted out with armour, guns and bellowing passengers, these giant specimens are walking bastions.
Using jingling bells, tasty fungal treats and an array of Painboy‑brewed serums, Zodgrod manages to propagate superior grots, snots and a variety of squig breeds.
Revelling in the rush of venting their built‑up powers, Weirdboys seek out the press of battle, intentionally supercharging their tortured brains and unleashing supernatural forces.
Painbosses augment themselves with piston‑driven supa‑legz, monowheels and the like to deliver high‑speed doktorin’ and surgical care.
The typical Snakebite is gnarled, weather‑worn and garbed in beast‑hide leather. They are as traditional as Orks come, favouring low‑tech wargear over anything needlessly fiddly.
Successful hunt leaders are never short of a kunnin’ plan to flush out the prey. They ransack whatever the prey values, luring the quarry with no bolthole or gear to fall back on.
Obsessed with being the first to make a kill, some Beast Snaggas will press their Painbosses to bionikaly enhance their wounded Squighogs for an edge during the hunt.
For most Beast Snaggas, the life of a squig-riding nomad who lives off the land, hunts huge horrible monsters and clobbers anything that crosses his path has great appeal.
Even the densest Orks can wrap their heads around the concept of gathering in massive mobs, bellowing while charging headlong at the enemy, then beating the foe to a bloody pulp.
Spying the largest or most dangerous threats on the battlefield, Beast Snaggas chase them down with gleeful enthusiasm, mobs racing each other to claim the kill.
Beast Snaggas have many tales of the times they took on the biggest prey, clobbering them with so many blows that what was left was a crumpled mass of broken hide and squished innards
Numbers; brawn; swarming runts and squigs; solid and reliable weapons and armour – these are what the more down‑to‑earth Orks believe win wars.
Some Imperial scholars claim that the power of the Waaagh! is the way in which Orks interact with the warp. Accurate or not, Oddboys act as a focal point for such tempestuous energy
It isn’t that Snakebites cannot use technology, but they employ know‑wotz only when they have to and won’t consider devices proppa until they’ve built up a patina of rust and oil.
A seemingly immortal bladefighter of superlative skill and egregious ego, Lucius has funnelled lifetimes of experience into raising his swordsmanship to supernatural superiority.
Arrogant slaughterer and swordmaster supreme, Lucius seeks out the most skilled of the foe's champions, followed by the Faultless to whom he promises untold sensations.
Possessed of an infernal arrogance and physical perfection, Xarahan prides itself upon its martial prowess, seeking nothing but to test itself against the greatest champions.
Towering over the mortals it leads to battle, Xarahan shares the Dark Prince's gifts through visions of excess and obsession. But such power is not given without a price.
Leading the Callous Blades to uncounted victories with towering arrogance, Lord Kaphrael singles out the enemy's champions, inflicting a gory demise upon his chosen foes.
Lord Kaphrael views the battlefield as an exhibition arena, dominating through martial prowess and an inexhaustible supply of sadistic imagination and bio-stimmulants.
Known to mortals as the handmaidens of Slaanesh, these daemons are a mixture of the beautiful and the monstrous, made all the more disturbing by the visceral clash of both.
Consumed by an obsessive desire to experience sensation in all its forms, Infractors hurl into battle with great sweeps and violent thrusts of their razor-sharp blades.
Tormentors echo the tactically adaptable squads that were once the mainstay of the Emperor's Children Legion before the horrors of the Heresy, striking with salvoes of explosive bolts.
Leading the Daemonettees, Alluresses delight in the carnage of battle, weaving around enemies' clumsy blows as they shrill and sigh their delight amidst swift-taloned slaughter.
The Glittering Myriad have carved a reputation for blindingly swift armoured assaults. Their Infractors are rampantly deployed into the battlefield, ready to indulge in violence.
Among the myriad warbands of the Emperor's Children, few revel in the enemy's agony as the Konstrictus do, leaving the battlefields as gouged victims crawl around fleshy bonfires.
Infractors vie with each other to carve the most visceral trail of destruction, viewing the battlefield as a stage gifted by Slaanesh with beings who exist only to be sliced apart.
Clad in garish power armour and clutching over-ornamented guns, Tormentors are aggressive front-line troops who revel in the gory deaths they inflict upon their enemies.
Chaos Spawn of Slaanesh hurl themselves into battle with reckless abandon, quivering with delight as they tear their opponents apart with mutant claws and sinuous tentacles.
These hedonistic worshippers of Slanesh are inured to most stimuli and seek to unleash the most cacophonous destruction to stir their jaded senses.
The Threnodic Choir orchestrate their battles with wailing harmonies that can destabilise tectonic plates, rendering the enemy an easy target for their endless sound barrage.
Granted power by daemonic patrons, the Flawless Blades strive to entertain their malefic masters with peerless swordplay and by inflicting vile and visceral death upon their foes.
Blastmasters focus a throbbing bass note into an explosive crescendo that can burst eyeballs, rupture organs and deliquesce the hardened armour of tanks.
Debased suits of Terminator armour offer Emperor's Children the raw power to bludgeon their way through swarms of lesser foes and the ability to endure apocalyptic attacks.
Leading Infractor squads seething with cocktails of stimulants, Obsessionists only care that their next fight is more bloody, extreme and sensationally wanton than the last.
Tormentors obsess over their ranged weapons. Most fetishise their boltguns, taking gratification in having mastered the symbolic weapon and raised its use to an art form
These chimerical daemon beasts manifest with arachnid, equine and reptilian traits. Their instincts for hunting down anything that promises to scream and hurt are preternatural.
Noise Marines served amongst Traitor Legions and Renegade Chapters, but they are most widespread amongst the Emperor's Children where they originated and were known as Kakophoni.
Envied and feared in equal parts, Veldras' speed and razor-sharp blades have claimed more heads than entire regiments, seeking nothing but the exhilarant joy of bloodshed.
Leading the Fiend packs, Blissbringers dissect their prey with oversized claws and immense strength, exposing nerves and organs to more invasive abuse.
Leading squads of Noise Marines, Disharmonists orchestrate riotous destruction by saturating the war zone with bursts of shattering noise and thrumming waves of aural destruction.
Ostentatious show-offs, Flawless Blade Champions dazzle and delight their fellow hedonists with displays of excessive bladework, haughty vigour and exposing themselves to danger.
The Sorcerers of the Emperor's Children delight in nothing but toying with their foes, for each gruesome kill they make is an offering to Slaanesh and promises a reward of power.
Known by his horrific, storming assaults in his baroque armour, Malgarash has honed his skills in his heavy weapons through millennia of pitiless, unstoppable slaughter.
Eager and impetuous of spirit, Emperor's Children Chaos Rhinos roar with barely contained anticipation as they thunder into the midst of battle to unload their cargo of warriors.
Terminator Champions arrogantly lord their power over others. Paranoia often takes root in those with power, leading them to obsessively re-establish their elite status.
Lords Kakophonist direct their excruciating aural barrages in atonal dirges, weakening physical matter by shaking chemical and atomic bonds with eldritch vibration.
The Konstrictus are glorious artisans and Turyan is no exception. The Prismatic Pyre erected on the sites of their victories is comprised of the eyeballs of those they leave alive.
Lords Exultants possess sensory enhancements, allowing them to experience the thrill of battle on a higher level, driving them to slaughter their foes in exquisitely lurid fashion.
Obsessed with lethal sonic destruction, Varius sculpted his entire body to further his art. With his band of Noise Marines, he conducts an orchestra of discordant slaughter.
Survivor of the Long War, this former Kakophoni's senses are so dulled that it hears none but the most devastating sounds, now cursed to rejoice in the most faint stimuli only.
Maulerfiends of the Emperor's Children possess a ravenous appetite for carnage and are empowered by the agonies inflicted upon them.
Heldrakes soar the skies, picking enemy aircraft apart with obsessive precision and malicious glee, only to descend and slaughter the enemy on the ground once the skies are clear.
Only the most debased and skilled warriors achieve daemonhood, and only a scant few are blessed with winged daemonic forms that long to inflict the most exquisite of agonies.
These tracked monstrosities purr and thrum with pleasure as they unleash booming volleys of destruction, stopping only to disgorge bands of warriors into the midst of the fighting.
Where the Emperor's Children indulge, the power of Slaanesh empowers those in its thrall. Only those who prove themselves the deadliest will gain the approval they seek.
The daemons of Slaanesh are not bound by the laws of reality, fading in and out of existence at will.
Emperor's Children warbands have claimed multiple bases, building fortresses and tributes to their greatness and luring tides of warp-spawned entities ready to spread violence.
Their ingrained desire for sensation in all its forms sees the Emperor's Children move rapidly across the battlefield as they attempt to satiate their hunger for fresh experience.
The Emperor's Children revel in every sensation - even ones that would slay lesser mortals outright
Through Slaanesh's favour, these warriors have defied death more than once and each time have been agonisingly resurrected to offer more souls to their patron.
The Emperor's Children are consummate raiders, eager to satiate their lust for sensation amid battle and falling upon their foes with impossible swiftness and inhuman grace.
The armoured transports of the Emperor's Children are a testament to the debased nature of those who ride within them.
Masters of mechanised assaults, the Emperor's Children leap from their daemonically tainted vehicles to fall upon the foe with blade, bolter and bizarre cocktails of stimms.
The Emperor's Children traverse the battlefield with their pupils dilated by exotic stimm cocktails, flesh scarred and sculpted by self-inflicted tortures
Only the most debased champions of Slaanesh may gain the Dark Prince's favour. Yet none hold it for long, for there's always another who seeks to wrest it from their rivals.
The audible noise that enemies detect is like the growl of a hungry god, so deep and powerful that the ground trembles, while eyes, eardrums and internal organs judder and rupture.
With a desire for perfection and superiority, some Emperor's Children warlords strike desperate pacts with daemonic powers, wagering their souls for power beyond measure.
Consumed by their own pride, the Emperor's Children seek to prove their prowess in myriad forms of combat, seeking out enemy champions to gruesomely humble in single combat.
Some warriors appear specially favoured by the Dark Prince, their boons of power a reward for committing ever viler deeds in honour of their patron.
Consumed by their obsessive desire for revenge, the Emperor's Children surge into oncoming fusillades.
Some Emperor's Children warriors demonstrate exquisite fighting form. Those who lock swords with these obsessive warriors do so at their peril.
Wherever the Emperor's Children tread, reality is torn asunder and through the veil pour the daemons of Slaanesh, their lithe forms at once repulsive and alluring.
When the Emperor's Children march to war, a barrage of sensations fills the arena. Air shivers in fearful expectation, and the land rifts as fortifications shatter into pieces.
The puissant champions of excess have inflicted deaths beyond count. The more extravagant and luridly violent the kill, the greater the Dark Prince's appreciation.
Essence-drums boil with narcotic rapture, distilling torment brewed from pain, each elixir tailored for transcendent violence, speed and ecstasy.
Pain is but the first note. The Emperor's Children armaments are as much weapons as they are instruments for a symphony of agony to please the Dark Prince.
The throne hums with echoes of worship and woe. Lured by their egomaniacal desires, warband members flock to it, seeking to to claim it and exert their will over those beneath them.
A discordant climax engulfs the battlefield, enrapturing the Emperor’s Children in ecstatic abandon while interlopers unfit to grasp such exquisite ruin are staggered.
An early release of the stimm substances might prove toxic to the foot soldier, but the lack of chemical stimmuli shall surely drive the motivation of the Dark Prince followers down.
When the daemonic energies burst out of control, no mortal soul is safe from the rapacious excess of empyric energy.
Phoenix Lord of the Warp Spiders, Lhykhis embodies Khaine's willingness to risk all to defeat the foe. Fearless of the Warp, Lhykhis traverses its helish depths with precision.
Lhykhis strikes like an ambush predator from the Empyrean, sowing murderous bloodshed amongst their foes before vanishing again into the web of the Warp.
The ritual armament of the Warp Spider is the death spinner, an exotic and highly advanced weapon that extrudes a cloud of razor-sharp monofilament wire and hurls it to the enemy.
The Warp Spiders take their name from the tiny crystalline arachnoids that crawl throughout a craftworld’s infinity circuit and Dome of Crystal Seers.
Armed with their signature Spinneret rifle, Orian braves the Warp to attack the enemy before fading away in the blink of an eye, lascerating foes with lethal accuracy one at a time.
Rapid target acquisition is the speciality of the Warp Spiders, materialising into realspace and slaying their unsuspecting foes in a storm of monofilament threads.
Farseers have become adept at reading future events, seeing the many strands of fate ahead of their people and the consequences of following each one
These sleek skimmers offer a perfect compromise between the speed of a jetbike and the heavier Aeldari armament, evincing incredible grace as their seated gunners blast the enemy.
Expert combatants and battle seers, these mounted Farseers flow around weapon blasts and blade thrusts with a natural grace that makes their foes seem predictable and slow.
Autarchs have long trodden the Path of the Warrior, and apply their strategic brilliance and sublime martial skill to their command of the Asuryani warhosts.
Ahnakh-Yth, the Weaver, who once watched over the Asuryani from her cosmic web, created the warp spiders who protect the Infinity Circuit from the intrusions of the Great Enemy.
The Aeldari have already seen how best to lay low each enemy and strike in the sure knowledge the foe cannot evade their terrible fate.
Farseers deliver prophetic orders, guiding their warriors to strike at crucial junctures of fate and causality. Their every pronouncement spells the doom of their foes.

Señor de la Guerra del Caos
Forja de la Mente de la Progenie
Nacido en las ciudades subterráneas de Calth, Uriel Ventris logró el mando de la 4ª Compañía y Flota del Capítulo, convirtiéndose en uno de los mayores héroes de los Ultramarines.
Pocas cosas escapan a la visión de Tigurius. Incluso para los Capitanes del Capítulo, es una figura misteriosa, poseedor de un conocimiento mayor incluso que los archivos del Imperio.
Desde los tiempos de la Gran Cruzada, los Ultramarines han estado entre las fuerzas más renombradas del Imperio, acumulando incontables distinciones de batalla a lo largo de los milenios.

El regreso de Guilliman durante uno de los momentos más oscuros de la humanidad devolvió un atisbo de esperanza a los corazones de la humanidad, encendiendo una luz que guiaría al Imperio hacia una nueva era.
La estricta adhesión de los Ultramarines al Codex Astartes es lo que hace al Capítulo una de las fuerzas más organizadas del Imperio.

Después de la revisión del Codex Astartes por parte de Guilliman, se reintrodujo el rango de Teniente. Los Tenientes ahora lideran a sus hermanos de batalla como lo hicieron durante la Herejía de Horus.
Aunque famoso como general, Marneus Calgar no es ajeno al valor personal. El Señor de Macragge lidera con el ejemplo, inspirando a sus guerreros desde el corazón de las líneas enemigas.
A menudo se considera a Calgar como la voluntad de la humanidad de resistir y triunfar hecha carne. Firme y decidido, liderará la lucha desde el frente hasta que las estrellas se enfríen.
Desde que ganó su apodo al desfigurar a Krugg el Tirano en un duelo por el liderazgo, la forma de luchar absolutamente brutal de Grukk se ha vuelto aún peor, para terror de sus enemigos.
Para demostrar su valía ante los ojos de sus brutales y astutos dioses, el poderoso Ghazghkull ha reunido el Waaagh más grande registrado en milenios.

La fuerza y la brutalidad son primordiales en la kultura Orko, donde cualquier discusión está destinada a provocar una pelea. Ghazghkull es el mayor debatiente orko, no habiendo perdido nunca una discusión.
Ocasionalmente , los Jefes de Guerra Orkos que veneran a Morko, el más astuto de los dioses Orkos, piensan en sus planes de batalla antes de lanzarse de cabeza a la lucha.
Los Orkos nunca dejan de crecer. Los orkos más grandes tienden a gobernar sobre los más pequeños, habiendo logrado la victoria en muchas batallas y sobrevivido violentos desafíos a su posición.
Los Orkos creen que Ghazghkull recibe mensajes de Gorko y Morko en persona, y que con él al mando del 'Gran Waaagh' volverán verdes a las estrellas.
Después de las muchas peleas de Ghazghkull con el Comisario Yarrick en Armageddon, Ghazghkull dejó el mundo infestado de Pieles Verdes dispersos y juró volver algún día.
Conocido simplemente como 'El Jefe' para su Escuadrón Vulcha, Zagstruk inspira un asombro casi fanático entre las Tropaz de Azalto, que hacen cola para seguir sus órdenes anunciadas a grito.
Es la naturaleza simple y resistente de la sociedad Orko lo que los eleva de una civilización de meras bestias matonas a una amenaza conquista-mundos, casi imparable.

Los Mekánikoz y Matazanoz pueden ser realmente colaborativos. Los Mekánikoz fabrican caminantes de combate conocidos como Dreznauts, luego los Matazanoz trabajan con ellos para conectar a los 'voluntarios' a las máquinas de guerra.
Las estrellas hablan de lo que está por venir. Leyéndolas Orikan ha adivinado el futuro de los Necrones y, una vez que estén en la alineación correcta, finalmente abrazará su verdadero destino.

Las palabras y acciones de los Cronomantes tienen un gran peso, ya que el conocimiento del futuro fluye a través de ellos. El futuro es caprichoso, pero las estrellas guiarán a los Necrones a una nueva edad dorada.
Incontables legiones y máquinas de guerra a su mando, listas para devastar al enemigo en un abrir y cerrar de ojos. Así es como los Señores Supremos Necrones reclamarán la Galaxia.
Enterrados durante millones de años, los Necrones durmieron a lo largo de eones. Ahora volviendo a la vida por toda la galaxia, sus imparables Legiones están resurgiendo.
Hace eones, una gran guerra contra los Aeldari obligó a los Necrones a afrontar un período de sueño. Ahora llega a su fin, y así se restaurarán las antiguas dinastías gobernantes.
Imotekh tiene como objetivo restaurar el Imperio Necrón a su antigua gloria. Solo cuando las dinastías se unan, comenzará de nuevo la dominación Necrón sobre los seres inferiores.
Después de tomar el trono de una nobleza centrada en sus propias disputas insignificantes, Imotekh moldeó el destino de su dinastía, asegurando su dominio sobre las razas menores.
El título de Némesor es pesado. Incluso tras las secuelas de la revivificación, Zahndrekh sigue siendo uno de los mayores estrategas Sautekh, y un campeón de su código dinástico.
A través de su avanzado conocimiento de la ciencia y la tecnología, los Criptecnólogos Necrones manipulan muchas de las fuerzas primordiales del universo para producir efectos de apariencia mágica.
La llegada del Reclamamundos presagia un destino fatal para cualquier enemigo. Es él quien proclama la muerte de los mundos, y él quien atraviesa con su lanza tanto a ciudadanos como a guerreros.

Fiel a sus orígenes de los Portadores de la Palabra, el don dela palabra de Sylar va más allá de la imaginación mortal. Con sus encantamientos, Hexscorn canaliza poderes demoníacos a aquellos bajo su mando.
La Legión Negra se formó a partir de las huestes de muchas bandas de guerra y comandantes. Todos juraron lealtad a Abaddon, quien los lidera con dominio absoluto.

El Ojo del Terror se convirtió en el santuario de las Legiones Traidoras después de la Herejía de Horus, y en un lugar en el que la Legión Negra reúne a sus fuerzas en preparación para una Cruzada Negra.

De la vergüenza y la sombra refundidos, en negro y oro renacidos. Las Fuerzas del Caos vieron en Abaddon a un nuevo Señor de la guerra para liderarlos a reclamar la victoria final que se les negó hace tanto tiempo.
La última de las Cruzadas Negras de Abaddon terminó con la destrucción de Cadia y la apertura de la Gran Fisura, una enorme brecha en la realidad que partió al Imperio en dos.
Después de la 13ª Cruzada Negra, Abaddon se convirtió en el amo de una desgarrada mitad del reino de la Humanidad que, dijo, era mucho más territorio del que Horus jamás conquistó y mantuvo.
Hubo un tiempo en que el Ojo de Horus representaba la vigilancia eterna del Emperador. Esos días se han ido, y ahora es un símbolo de temor y desesperación.
Desde el final de la Herejía de Horus, Abaddon ha reunido a las fuerzas dispersas del Caos bajo su estandarte. Está decidido a reclamar venganza contra el Falso Emperador.
Las habilidades premonitorias de Anvirr lo llevaron a Vigilus, donde forjó una improbable alianza con Marneus Calgar para repeler una armada del Caos que amenazaba el futuro de los Aeldari.

Protectora del mundo astronave, Ghaelyn ha levantado su lanza contra la sombra y la llama una y otra vez, comandando las fuerzas de Saim-Hann en defensa de los santuarios Aeldari y los Mundos Vírgenes.
Cada miembro de una Hueste Salvaje de Saim-Hann anhela ser el primero en la lucha y reclamar la gloria de la primera sangre. Nada se interpondrá entre ellos y su presa.

Las estrellas están alineadas, y la luna carmesí indica que ha llegado la hora de la sangre y el choque de filos. Es hora de que la Hueste Salvaje se levante y cabalgue, hora de que la serpiente muerda.

Todos los Aeldari pueden manipular energías psíquicas hasta cierto punto. Gran parte de su equipo de guerra está vinculado empáticamente con el usuario, quien puede activarlo con un simple pensamiento.
La simbología de Saim-Hann recuerda a la Serpiente Cósmica, la criatura que se cree que existe tanto en los universos material y psíquico al mismo tiempo en la mitología Aeldari.

Casi todos los Saim-Hann pertenecen a un clan de Jinetes Salvajes, que cabalgan en escuadrones de motos a reacción compuestos por parientes de sangre, luciendo estandartes con las runas de su clan mientras derriban las líneas enemigas.
Es una dolorosa ironía que, en la interminable búsqueda de supervivencia de los Aeldari, los mismos civiles que los ejércitos luchan por proteger, se vean obligados a tomar las armas a menudo.
Con una agilidad y precisión impactantes, las huestes de Eliac Zephyrblade caen como las lanzas de Khaine contra el corazón de aquellos que se atreven a dañar el mundo astronave.
El poder psíquico hecho forma, el Neurótropo no solo actúa como un nodo sináptico, sino también como un pulsante nexo psíquico que canaliza fuerzas arcanas para succionar la vida de sus enemigos.
Los Tervigones aseguran que el asalto nunca termine, despertando a los Termagantes que llevan en su abdomen, y desgarrando a los enemigos con sus garras.
La quitina endurecida que recubre las formas de los Tiránidos ha demostrado ser anormalmente duradera. Pocos pueden detener al enjambre una vez que ha decidido devorar un planeta.

La Flota Enjambre Leviatán ha extendido sus tentáculos a través de la Galaxia, lista para consumir todo en su camino. Todos los que se encuentran con ellos temen que no haya forma de detener al Gran Devorador.
Asentándose como un vasto y terrible manto en innumerables mundos, la Sombra en la Disformidad es un fenómeno de pesadilla que anuncia la llegada de las flotas enjambre Tiránidas.
La Mente Enjambre es la conciencia colectiva de su especie, una inteligencia insondable creada por la presencia psíquica de miles de millones de Tiránidos todos conectados entre sí.
Las armas características del Señor de la Horda pueden atravesar el adamantium y los campos protectores como si nada. Atacan con tal velocidad que pocos tienen si quiera la oportunidad de golpear.
El Señor de la Horda, una magnánima amenaza galáctica, es la criatura sináptica más poderosa jamás conocida, inmortal y tan antigua como la misma especie Tiránida.

La primera advertencia que la mayoría de los mundos reciben sobre el acercamiento de los Tiránidos es la Sombra en la Disformidad. Esta señal psíquica se adelanta a las flotas enjambre como una asfixiante niebla metafísica.
Un ataque Tiránido es un espectáculo aterrador a presenciar. Enormes enjambres de monstruos voraces fluyen a través de la tierra, masacrando todo a su paso.
Desde la oscuridad entre las estrellas fluye una marea de pesadillas vivientes. Su sombra es el sudario funerario de las civilizaciones. Su hambre es la muerte de los mundos.
El Sector T'au es el faro brillante de la luz del Bien Supremo, su mayor asentamiento de cultura y sabiduría y un sinónimo de excelencia militar.
El XV8 Crisis proporcionó el chasis prototipo para varias exoarmaduras más avanzadas, incluyendo el XV86 Estrella de Hielo con su capacidad de vuelo trans-atmosférico.
Los adherentes del T'au'va realizan a gusto increíbles esfuerzos, soportan dificultades impactantes y dan sus vidas sin pensarlo dos veces para el avance del Bien Supremo.
Los T'au creen que el mensaje del Bien Supremo debe ser llevado a todos, por lo que siguen expandiendo las fronteras de su imperio y estableciendo nuevos sistemas colonizados llamados sectores.

Desarrolladas en secreto en la Estación J'ka'vo y cada una pilotada por un Shas'vre seleccionado a mano, las Exoarmaduras XV-95 se embarcaron en numerosas operaciones encubiertas antes de su presentación oficial.
Los Kroot son guerreros belicosos y sedientos de sangre. Aunque su agresión primitiva es vista con desagrado por los T’au, tal salvajismo inherente los convierte en tropas de choque efectivas.
La Casta Etérea se distingue de su pueblo. Gobiernan a los T'au como un adulto sabio y paciente podría guiar a jóvenes enérgicos y descarriados para que alcancen su verdadero potencial.
Shadowsun ha convertido en icónica la avanzada Exoarmadura Stalker XV22, llegando a ser tan hábil en el manejo de la XV22 que se ha vuelto como una segunda piel blindada para ella.
La Galaxia es despiadada. Si uno busca sobrevivir a sus peligros, debe estar preparado para superar innumerables desafíos. ¿Podrás resistir a los caprichos del destino?
Cada avance en la guerra requiere una prueba de campo adecuada, y aquellos dispuestos a ayudar a expandir los límites de lo posible se elevarán en la gracia del Dios Máquina.
La historia está dictada por causa y efecto. Las ondas enviadas por eventos de eras pasadas aún se pueden sentir en toda la Galaxia. ¿Resonarán también tus acciones a través de la eternidad?
Algunos traidores se han entregado completamente al servicio de los Dioses Oscuros, y están tan perdidos en la condenación que apenas se parecen a los guerreros que una vez fueron.
Las oraciones del Apóstol Oscuro llenan los corazones de sus seguidores con odio, quienes se lanzan con fanática fuerza para derribar a sus enemigos en los nombres de los Dioses Oscuros.
La Disformidad existe como fuente de poder ilimitado y condenación eterna. Tal poder siempre ha tentado a los incautos, los desesperados y los ambiciosos hacia sus profundidades sin fondo.

Las conjuraciones más corruptas se pueden lograr con energía demoníaca. Los hechiceros pueden haber sido psíquicos desde el nacimiento; otros pueden ser guerreros a quienes un patrón demoníaco les otorga tal poder.
Las Hermanas de la Orden de Nuestra Señora Mártir son las liberadoras de la santa justicia del Dios Emperador, los temidos instrumentos de su voluntad a quienes ningún sacrificio es demasiado grande.
Para las Adepta Sororitas, el acto de luchar en defensa de su fe, contra los herejes que intentarían derribarla, se considera en sí mismo un sagrado honor.
Las Adepta Sororitas son una fuerza militar en cruzada que aplasta a los enemigos del Credo Imperial dondequiera que se encuentren, iluminando el reino del Emperador como un faro de fe.
Se dice que la sangre de los mártires es la semilla del Imperio. Donde cae, florecen la repugnancia y la venganza, y prosperan las furiosas represalias de los fieles.
En el sepulcro de la batalla, son los guerreros más santos del Dios Emperador. En el relicario de la guerra, donde se hacen los santos y la fe arde con más fuerza, son Su voluntad hecha manifiesta.
Los Kroot poseen una biología morfágica que les permite absorber rasgos genéticos de la carne que devoran. Los Formadores tienen un entendimiento instintivo de esta habilidad y cómo explotarla mejor.
Los Necrones reemplazaron su debilidad carnal con formas duraderas de metal viviente hace eones. Sin embargo, la biotransferencia también privó a la mayoría de los Necrones de su libre albedrío.
El Emperador protege a los fieles de la Corrupción que acecha en la oscuridad. Es bajo Su luz que las Sororitas avanzan con una voluntad indomable.
Declaradas por el eclesiárquico reinante del Adeptus Ministorum, las Guerras de Fe a menudo se convocan para buscar la Conquista de nuevo territorio o purgar a los Herejes del Credo Imperial.
Los preceptos de las Órdenes proclaman jubilosos que la sangre de los mártires es la fuerza vital del Imperium, haciendo que el sacrificio de sus Hermanas Caídas brille más en la hora más oscura.

Después de la derrota de los Ancestrales, cuando los C’tan estaban en su punto más débil tras ese conflicto titánico, los Necrones tomaron su venganza, destrozando y encarcelando a los dioses estelares traicioneros.

Los Capellanes son fogosos, estrictos y se enfurecen rápidamente ante el enemigo odiado. A pesar de su semblante sombrío, los Capellanes se preocupan profundamente por el bienestar espiritual de sus hermanos.
Las Compañías de Batalla se dividen frecuentemente en dos semi-compañías, cada una bajo el mando directo de un Teniente, un táctico extremadamente capaz y un guerrero altamente habilidoso.
Las armas bólter han sido sinónimo de los Marines Espaciales desde antes incluso de la Gran Cruzada. Innumerables enemigos han caído por sus rondas explosivas, conocidas como bólters.
A la 4ª Compañía le recae el deber de defender el vasto Ultramar de las depredaciones de los innumerables herejes, alienígenas y monstruosidades que desean verlo arder en llamas.
Orgullosos aliados del Imperio T'au, el equipo rústico y la apariencia salvaje de los Kroot representan perfectamente su temible habilidad en combate.
"¡Alabad a los Hijos de las Estrellas! ¡Alabad al Maestro de Abajo! ¡Alabad a la libertad, la liberación y la ascensión!"

Los Cultos Genestealer están dominados por un Patriarca a través del vínculo sináptico conocido como Mente de la Progenie. A medida que el Culto crece, su Mente de la Progenie se convierte en un faro psíquico para la colmena Tiránida.

Acechan en las sombras, insidiosos, pacientes. Día a día extienden su maldición. Absorben fuerzas y hunden sus tentáculos cada vez más profundo, hasta que por su palabra se despliega la sangre y el horror.

Cada secta genética engendra espontáneamente individuos notables con habilidades concentradas cuya presencia allana el camino hacia la ascensión, cada uno moldeado por el mundo y la cultura que parasitan.
Desde la primera infección, generaciones sucesivas nacerán dentro del culto. Los descendientes nacidos en la cuarta generación son Genestealers Puros que reiniciarán el ciclo.
Mediante la astucia y la fortuna, los Cultos Genestealer extienden sus tentáculos hasta los rangos más altos de las fuerzas militares que debieran protegerse de ellos.
Cuando estalla el alzamiento, el Patriarca deja su trono en medio de sus Piscinas de Génesis y emerge de las sombras. El monstruoso y parasítico semidiós lidera el asalto final.
Los descendientes nacidos de la cuarta generación son Genestealers puros. Sus padres perciben a su progenie de pesadilla como querubines benditos, y se sacrificarían por ellos sin dudarlo.
La gente de los mundos astronave se adhiere a un conjunto de normas conocido como el Camino, o el Ai’elethra, dominando sus impulsos a través de la rígida disciplina emocional del Camino.
Los Mekánikos sienten el impulso de trastear y experimentar constantemente con nuevas ideas. Con gusto harán molifikaziones para otros Orkos a cambio de pago en dientes o chatarra saqueada.

Titus es un hábil guerrero en el campo de batalla, y su deber le enfrenta a menudo a adversidades imposibles, que sólo puede superar gracias a su furia, determinación y afiladas habilidades de combate.

Debido a su incapacidad para proteger los códigos dinásticos al final de la Guerra en el Cielo, se encargó a los Triarcas Pretorianos que vigilaran los Mundos Necrópolis dormidos durante el Gran Sueño.
Ramatekh emana una presencia que atormenta el alma. La promesa del fin de la vida es tan explícita en su escalofriante mirada que pocos pueden reunir la fuerza de voluntad para evadirla.

Los Criptecnólogos reúnen ejércitos enteros de construcciones artificiales y soldados sin alma para lograr su objetivo. Seguidores ciegamente leales, estos autómatas son guiados por el antiguo genio de sus amos.
Los regimientos y sus mundos de origen glorifican las nobles victorias, últimas resistencias y épicas cruzadas de sus guerreros, bordándolas en gloriosos y asombrosos tapices.
El Imperium se enfrenta a muchos horrores. Los soldados del Astra Militarum son el Martillo del Emperador, y por sus acciones serán destruidos los enemigos de la Humanidad.
Obliterando a los enemigos del Imperium con explosivas granadas, los regimientos blindados son una respuesta efectiva y a veces excesiva a la invasión y la insurrección.
Son la materia prima sobre la que gira la maquinaria bélica del Imperium. Son el yunque sobre el que se forjan las victorias. Son el escudo tras el que perdurará la Humanidad.

Durante La Forja, mientras nuevos sistemas eran incorporados al dominio Imperial, las Tropas de Choque de Cadia impartieron su disciplina y doctrina militar a los líderes de los mundos recién colonizados.
Con rifle, cañón y la valentía humana, rechazan horrores pesadillescos. Son los soldados del Astra Militarum, y en sus muertes no registradas se manifiesta el deber inmaculado.

La Galaxia es despiadada, pero los pocos valientes se levantan para reclamar su lugar en ella. Otorgado a aquellos que comandaron sus mazos hacia la victoria durante la etapa de Acceso Anticipado de Warpforge.

Los Cadianos tienen fe en la fuerza de la Humanidad, pero no dependen únicamente de las oraciones para su salvación. En su hora más oscura, enfrentan al mal no suplicando, sino disparando su arma hasta el amargo final.

La mayoría de los Asuryani se unen voluntariamente a la guerra. Conocidos como Aspectos Guerreros, cada rama del Camino tiene su propio estilo de lucha único y refleja una faceta única del dios Khaine.
Los Espectros Aullantes anuncian su llegada con un grito que hiela la sangre, amplificado por sus máscaras de Banshee, infligiendo daño severo a los sistemas nerviosos centrales de sus enemigos.

Cuando Asurmen levantó a los originales Guerreros de la Senda, se convirtió en el primero de los Asurya. La primera en aprender bajo su tutela fue Jain Zar, una espadachina Aeldari famosa por su velocidad y ferocidad.

La raza humana lleva profundas cicatrices en su psique colectiva de la Era de los Conflictos. La humanidad sobrevivió a sus estragos fragmentada y desesperada, emergiendo como una especie muy cambiada.
Rodeadas de luz sagrada y poseídas de serenidad divina, las Hermanas de la Rosa Sagrada son la calma en el centro de una tormenta violenta.
Las Hermanas de la Rosa Sagrada reflejan el sereno semblante de su Matriarca, Arabella, famosa por su naturaleza tranquila incluso frente al horror.
Las Órdenes de la Adepta Sororitas se dividen entre el Convento Sanctorum, basado en Ophelia VII, y el Convento Prioris, que fue construido dentro del Palacio de la Eclesiarquía en la Sagrada Terra.
La Adepta Sororitas ejecuta a cualquiera que exprese dudas sobre la seguridad del Imperio. Las Hermanas de la Rosa Sagrada han luchado contra los enemigos de la fe con resolución de espíritu.
Una venerada reliquia espada que una vez sostuvo la misma Santa Arabella, Aveline Aboyé ahora maneja la Espina de la Rosa Blanca con resolución contra los enemigos a los que juró vencer.
Los Adeptus Astartes son post-humanos fuertemente aumentados; productos de años de arduo entrenamiento, cirugía agonizante y psico-indoctrinación que no todos los reclutas sobrevivirán.

Los imponentes escudos tormenta de los Bladeguard son el trabajo de muchas generaciones de siervos, y los generadores de campo de fuerza que contienen protegen el alma del portador tanto como su carne.

Entre los sangrientos destinos de un campeón del Caos se encuentra el internamiento en el sarcófago de un Bruto Infernal, un imponente motor de carnicería con el poder de fuego de un tanque y la sed de sangre de un daemon.

En cada nivel de la organización de su Capítulo, los Ángeles Oscuros tienen una desconcertante variedad de antiguos rituales y tradiciones liderados por los Capellanes de los Ángeles Oscuros, como la Fiesta de la Maldición.

Reconsagrados al servicio del Imperio después de eludir su riguroso escrutinio, los Ángeles Oscuros pusieron en marcha un plan para asegurar la supervivencia de la Legión. Nadie podía dudar de su resolución o compromiso.

Creían que sus hermanos traidores habían perecido en la destrucción de Caliban, los Bibliotecarios de los Ángeles Oscuros descubrieron más tarde las firmas psíquicas de los Caídos, revelando que aún vivían.
Después de la destrucción de Caliban, los Ángeles Oscuros se consideraban completamente culpables, y que si alguien se enteraba de lo ocurrido, la Primera Legión sería declarada Excomulgar Traitoris.

Desde los tiempos de la Gran Cruzada, los hijos de Caliban han estado en la vanguardia de algunas de las guerras más significativas de la galaxia, y han desangrado a sus enemigos en numerosas zonas de guerra.

La historia más profunda de los Ángeles Oscuros está envuelta en misterio, no solo debido a que se remonta a miles de años en el pasado, sino también por los Maestros y Veteranos de los Ángeles Oscuros que la oscurecen deliberadamente.

Los orgullosos guerreros de los Ángeles Oscuros se niegan obstinadamente a aceptar la derrota. Descendientes de la Primera Legión, se sitúan en primera línea entre los Capítulos de los Marines Espaciales.
Los Ángeles Oscuros equipan a toda su 1ª Compañía - el Ala de Muerte - con armadura Exterminador, armas de energía envueltas en relámpagos y altos escudos reliquia.

Los Ángeles Oscuros fueron la Primera Legión. Ninguna otra hermandad de Marines Espaciales ha servido al Emperador durante tanto tiempo como ellos. Firmes defensores de la Humanidad, son despiadados en el ataque y obstinados en la defensa.
Primordial en los esfuerzos del Chacal está el Chacal Alphus. Poseen la constitución para viajar durante días, planificando y ejecutando el disparo perfecto para eliminar objetivos clave.

Ya sea extrayendo riquezas de pozos infernales o trabajando en forjas, los fieles se han convertido en expertos en el manejo de las descomunales herramientas industriales que ahora manejan como armas.

El impulso telepático del Patriarca implanta el verdadero objetivo en su cría de la camada: romper las líneas enemigas y acumular inteligencia militar vital. Luego, el culto causa estragos con los escombros manipulados.
Tropas de asalto de choque sin igual, los Vástagos Tempestus son soldados de élite utilizados para llevar a cabo misiones que la Guardia Imperial regular no puede lograr sola.
Desde jóvenes, los Vástagos Tempestus son adoctrinados en la lealtad y la rápida ejecución de sus deberes. Poseen la tenacidad para emprender las misiones más duras y hacer el trabajo.
Los Aquilones están entrenados para caer justo en medio de la lucha. Su extenso acondicionamiento les permite mantenerse enfocados incluso durante las inserciones más feroces.

Algunos Orkos abandonar sus tribus en busca de lo salvaje. Los enclaves Orkos aislados a menudo degeneran a un estado más primitivo y se dedican a la cría de Garrapatos, convirtiéndose en Trinkabeztiaz.
El Garrapato indomable; la Malabestia de Skrapmud– Mordizkazoz se convirtió en la montura de Mozrog con una reputación de ser la criatura más cruel y salvaje jamás vista.
A medio digerir pero aún con ganas de pelea, Mozrog Skragbad no solo caza bestias. Con un impresionante recuento de trofeos, siempre se siente impulsado a buscar presas más grandes.
Los Trinkabeztiaz crían innumerables variedades de Garrapatos: para montar;  para comer; para exprimir aceite; para enviar con glifos de mensajes garabateados apresuradamente...
Peligrosos e inestables, los Beztiambótikos son tratados como oráculos. Raramente lúcidos, deliran sobre visiones de presas y se pierden en los sentidos de los Garrapatos.
Después de diez milenios, los fragmentados Hijos del Emperador aún acechan a la galaxia en vibrantes bandas de guerra de imperiosa habilidad, estremecedor poder de fuego y ruinosos deseos.
La guerra es un arte empapado en sangre. Cada batalla es un lienzo fresco en el que la superioridad de los vástagos de Fulgrim se representa en sangre, vísceras y los gritos agonizantes del enemigo.
El arraigado deseo de los Hijos del Emperador por la sensación en todas sus formas les hace moverse rápidamente por el campo de batalla para saciar su hambre interminable de nuevas experiencias.
Cuando los Hijos del Emperador van a la guerra, es al estridente chillido de un conjunto de extravagantes armas sónicas que fragmentan la realidad y raspan los nervios de todos los que lo oyen.

El exceso y la obsesión son los dominios de Slaanesh. Los deseos insatisfechos y los sueños compulsivos son las grietas por las que se deslizan los susurros de Slaanesh, atrayendo a los mortales a su adoración.

Nacidos de la semilla genética de Fulgrim, la III Legión buscaba la perfección en la guerra. Endurecidos por una vida de conflicto incesante, su búsqueda de excelencia se deslizó hacia el exceso y la condenación.
Los Hijos del Emperador buscan esencias exóticas para alimentar sus obsesiones. Encontradas en la carne, la mente y el alma, cosechan el tormento para destilar sustancias exquisitas.

Buscando cometer atrocidades cada vez más depravadas para satisfacer sus monstruosos deseos, los guerreros de una banda de guerra pueden desollar la piel de sus víctimas con afiladas cuchillas o deslumbrante hechicería empyrica.
Ya sea sometiendo a un daemon a su voluntad o dominando a un campeón enemigo, los Señores Exultantes se deleitan en mostrar su superioridad y exponen los imperdonables defectos de sus enemigos.
Lhykhis encarna la disposición de Khaine de arriesgarlo todo para derrotar al enemigo. Se encuentra entre los Señores Fénix más activos, viajando lejos y ampliamente en defensa de los Asuryani.

Las Arañas de Disformidad desafían la disformidad para defender a los vivos, al igual que las diminutas criaturas de disformidad a las que deben su nombre se materializan cerca del Circuito Infinito para proteger a los muertos.
Las almas que pilotan los espectros constructos de Asuryani experimentan la realidad como un sueño, donde sus pensamientos, sentimientos y los de otros Aeldari son tan tangibles como el acero.

Los orgullosos guerreros de los Ángeles Oscuros se niegan obstinadamente a aceptar la derrota. Descendientes de la Primera Legión, se sitúan en primera línea entre los Capítulos de los Marines Espaciales.
La hora de la sangre y de los filos ha llegado.
Me pongo a prueba una y otra vez y, sin embargo, sigo venciendo.
Cada uno de tus viles actos conlleva una horrible consecuencia.
Siempre hay un camino. Siempre lo encuentro.
Nunca te enzarces en una batalla si no conoces el resultado.
Sé lo que es perderlo todo, y no fallaré.
Recorres un camino que te lleva a tu propia ruina.
Venid, guerreros, nuestra salvación no está aquí.
Las hebras del destino me han guiado hasta aquí.
Tu perdición se acerca, lo he presagiado.
Aunque esté manchado de rojo, debo recorrer este camino.
No pude ser doblegado en el pasado, y tampoco lo seré ahora.
Tu especie aún tiene muchos crímenes por los que responder.
Llegará nuestra venganza, pero primero debemos asegurar nuestra supervivencia.
Tu sola presencia corrompe lo que yace tras el velo.
Tu inmunda raza pagará por la tragedia de Hyperia.
